scores.why: The yardstick. It is the original CRT soul at full strength (halo, bloom, glowing dots), but it is all green on black, bright and contrasty, with nearly one hue everywhere. It is the page the owner asked to calm, and the family called it 'the Matrix'.

Best for the owner. Track Diagram's line language runs through every page: the Coming up track from a lit now lamp, the setup track, To do's timetable with a new lit 'now' stop, Chat hung from Vera's mark down to a lit ring, Status rails, ring-and-bracket heads, and a dot under the current page. The tube is switched back on only where it is live: the monitors glow like today's, the lamps and her screens bloom, and the lit track segment fades from the lamp. Everything else stays on grounded slate and steel. Still thick-cased monitors and an olive-brown setup tray.

The best-made listing system (one-line rows read to tabular facts, head columns that now say how each band stands, labelled nav) with the tube relit: the monitor halo is back to near today's, and so are the lamps and Send. It gains a Now rail on Coming up and a Chat thread to a lit ring, which the owner will like. The lines are still fewer than Track Diagram's (To do, Status and Plans have none), and the pewter monitor case is still heavy.

Track Diagram reset on a written five-step scale with a 17px body. The owner, who enjoys typesetting, would feel the calmer rhythm and better measure. But the tube stays at the parent's dimmer #74f0a3 and 0.81 screen, so it does not answer 'bring some of that back', and the phone titles now wrap to two lines.

Still the line art the owner called high style, carried with restraint through every page on grounded slate and steel. Side by side with its relit child, though, its thinner halo on the monitors and lamps reads as the soul turned down.

The strongest newcomer. It is a 1969 flight console: a readout strip at the top of Home, a flight-plan track with arcs between stops on Home and Plans, an annunciator panel on Status, a crew board of lamps on To do and a T-3 countdown for setup. The consoles are grounded grey, the radar glows fully and the lamps are lit green. It is fresh, period computing that keeps the CRT soul. Faults: tracked mono caps in the nav and legends, FIG captions as costume, and the Coming up list and Status lamps each shown twice.

Rails with the heads set into them, the Coming up track with its now lamp, the Chat thread and full relit glow: the owner's line language and light together. Faults: the setup tray is filled olive-bronze (brown, which the owner rejects), the kind-tinted plates are warm, and To do is still a card list.

The engraved line drawings standing on Home's rules (sunrise over hills, a clipboard, a jar of idea slips, a present) are charming, in the owner's favourite medium, with one thing in each section's colour. But they illustrate rather than draw structure, they live on Home only, dropping every icon costs recognition (the 'Speak' word replaces the mic), and the olive setup tray remains.

A grounded matte cockpit with its instruments lit, which is the right idea for the light. But the tracked mono caps heads and small legends are busy, there are no tracks or lines carrying order anywhere, and the blue outline for 'here' is more blue than it needs to be.

A good idea: the light is the data. Each page has one full-bloom P1 scope that draws its own plans, due dates or places, and pointing at a row lights its mark. Elsewhere the page is graphite print. But the tracks the owner loves are gone, replaced by generic column-headed tables, and on Home the trace's spikes say little at a glance.

The lit glass column with a green pool and a machine status line at its foot is real CRT soul. But blueprint-blue tiles on every row and head make it more blue than necessary, the paper-white 'here' block in the bar reads as disabled, and the column is mostly empty glass on Status, Plans and To do.
The docked glass column gives the green a clear home, but the raised indigo keys and blue buttons and tags spread blue across the desk. It has no line art, and the list rows are plain.

A written six-size scale and every dock as a console, which is coherent. But the banks of indigo and blue keys (the kind chips, the For bank) are the loudest thing on Ideas and To do, and the owner has said the blue is more than necessary. There is no line art.

Its data-drawn figures are line art with meaning (Status wiring, To do late bars), which the owner likes. But the cream 'here' cells in the bar glare, blue underlined links fill every row, and the CRT glow shrinks to the small figure plates.

The Home terminal, a big glowing tube holding Next up, the radar and the question with a cursor, has more CRT soul than anything this round. But the brown plastic cases and key row, the khaki title bands and the pastel pink and lilac tiles are the warm browns and pinks the owner has rejected.

The spine with NOW, NEXT and LATER stops through every page is line art the owner would enjoy, and the screens glow. But the pixel-font heads are toy-like, the chunky khaki-olive frames are the heavy plain boxes the owner dislikes, and berry pink marks 'now'.

Calm, large print, and a picture light over the monitor is a lovely touch. But the brass, olive and putty warmth works against the CRT motif, wide-tracked caps heads and one size for every word flatten the hierarchy, and there are no lines carrying order.

The listing is calm and grounded. Slate bands, a steel 'here' block and low-chroma kind keys hold up the bright green, and the thin brackets that drop from each head and turn under its band are close to the line work the owner praised. Next to its own Relit version (8.3) it has less glow, though: the tubes are dimmer (screen #74f0a3), and it has no Coming up rail and no Chat thread, so it carries less of the CRT feel and the tracks the owner asked for.

fixes.suggestion: Keep everything: the tracks, lamps, timetable margins, the lit 'now' stop and the relit tubes. (1) Take r11-mut-1's five-step type scale and 17px body. (2) Thin the monitor case, which the owner has twice called a too-dominant pewter slab: a 1px engraved rim with a fine inner groove, not a thick rounded frame. (3) Remove the olive-bronze fill from the setup tray; amber belongs in the rings and the edge only. (4) Take the kind tints off the Ideas cards (Restaurant reads brown, Show plum) and keep kind colour in the ring lamp. (5) Make the lit segment's fade toward the next stop visible at 1x; today it barely shows. (6) Label the right-hand nav icons (Memory, Family, Status, Settings) as Evening Listing Relit does. (7) Ship the views.task_row `late` flag so the amber stops on To do are real.

Keep the listing grammar, the head columns with their counts, the steel reverse block and the relit list. Carry the line language to the pages still without it: a timetable rail with a lit now lamp down To do (as Track Diagram does), a rail through Status's 'Who answers' chain, and a track on the Plans list. Dim the steel 'here' block one step so it never competes with #6dff9c. Thin the monitor bezel the same way as for r11-mut-4.

Keep the flight-plan track with its arcs, the Home readout strip, the annunciator, the crew board, the T-3 countdown and the lit radar: this is a period CRT computing language that fits the owner. Fix these: set the nav and the buttons in sentence case, not tracked mono caps. Drop the FIG captions, or keep one only where a drawing needs a key. Stop saying things twice: hang the Coming up plates from the arcs' stops and drop the separate list, and make the annunciator Status's summary with the three lists folded below it. Drop the screws. Tint the grey consoles a breath toward green-black. Keep violet only in the drawings, at lower chroma.

The engraved drawings standing on a rule are worth keeping. Make them a system: one on each page head (Plans, To do, Ideas, Status), in the same pewter hand with one thing in the section's colour. Bring the icons back to the bar and the phone's tab bar, and the mic glyph back to its button, for recognition. Replace the olive setup fill with an amber edge.

Keep the scope that draws each page's own data, with its full bloom and afterglow, and the hover that lights a row's mark. Graft it onto Track Diagram or Evening Listing rather than column-headed tables, so the tracks come back. On Home, name the four plan pulses or draw them as lit stops on a line, so the trace reads at a glance.

The Home terminal (one big glowing tube holding Next up, the radar and the question with a blinking cursor) and the contents list with leaders are worth developing. Put them in a graphite or slate case, not brown plastic, and turn the pastel number tiles into small lamps.

Keep the spine with its NOW, NEXT and LATER stops through every page. Keep pixel type for figures at most and set heads in a sans. Replace the chunky khaki frames with thin rules, and let NOW be the lit green lamp rather than berry pink.

judges.notes:
What I looked at: every strip, details strip and squint strip, the home, home-phone, chat, status, settings, login and to-do sheets, the squint sheet, and full-size shots of the leaders (their Next up monitors side by side at 1:1; Status and Chat for Track Diagram against its relit child).

The two relit mutants answer the owner's latest word best. At 1:1, r11-mut-4's and r11-idea-1's monitors have today's halo back, and their lamps and her screens bloom again. Everything else stays on grounded slate and steel, so the light falls on a short list. That makes the relit version of each parent clearly better than the parent for this lens.

Track Diagram Relit wins because it carries the line art the owner called "high style" onto every page and now lights it where it is live. Most of the owner's recurring faults survive in all the Track and Signal children:
- the thick pewter monitor case;
- the olive-bronze setup tray (brown);
- the warm kind tints on the idea plates.
Fix these in the next round.

The owner would want this breed: Track Diagram Relit's lines and light, Evening Listing's rows and head columns, and Large Setting's type scale.

Of the wild entrants, Flight Console is the one to develop. Its period instruments (readout strip, flight-plan arcs, annunciator, crew board) are fresh, grounded and keep the glow. It needs sentence case, no duplication and fewer captions.

Warm materials lost again in this lens:
- Videotex's brown plastic;
- Night Gallery's brass and olive;
- Pocket Timeline's khaki and berry.
The owner has said brown and pink work against the motif. Videotex's big Home tube is the best single CRT-soul idea of the round and should be tried in a cool case.

Blue-led entrants (Tuning Dock, Docked Terminal, Blueprint Terminal) still spend more blue than necessary on keys and tiles.

scores.why: The source of the soul: every lit thing has its full halo, the greeting has its pool, and the tubes bloom. But the glow is not scarce. Green runs through every icon, link and button and amber discs glow, so nothing jumps and the page reads as 'the Matrix'. It is the yardstick, not the goal.

The clearest statement yet of 'light is a list'. The now lamps are white-hot points in a breathing halo, and the track from the lamp to the next stop is lit, on Home's Coming up, To do's timetable and the Status chain alike. The tubes are at 1.0 with their spill, the chat hangs from her screen to a lit ring, and slate and steel stay matte everywhere else. Light reaches below the fold, and it means now.

The most meaningful phosphor on the panel. Each tube draws the family's own data: plans as pulses on a fortnight scope, due dates around a NOW line on To do, a spend meter, and a 'NO SIGNAL' flat trace on the 404. Each has bloom, a sweep and afterglow, and the rest is quiet print. In stills the resting pulses are faint and sparse, and the legend tables cramp on Status.

The most CRT-hearted first screen: you type the question on the glass under a blinking cursor, beside a large radar. The tube warms up from a line, and the key row shows an LED on the current key. Mosaic bands are true videotex graphics. It is let down by double-height VT323 on every heading off the glass, noisy dither blocks behind titles, a brown case and a 3574px Home, so it risks costume.

The tubes are back at full strength, the greeting pool and scanlines return, Status lamps glow as dots, and Chat ends in a lit ring. It is calm and grounded, and the listing works on every page. But below the fold Home is almost fully matte (only a tiny NOW), and the row afterglow cannot be seen, so the listing half feels unlit.

The halo is back on mind, Send and the lamps, the monitors bloom fully, and a now lamp opens the Coming up track. Light runs through Chat's glowing bubble edges, which spreads the glow to things that are not live.
The lit-versus-matte rule is well kept: tubes at full bloom, glowing lamps on dark slots, matte faceplates. But caps legends and dense plates make it read as an admin cockpit more than a warm tube.

Every page gets a real tube at 1.0 with a roll-bar power-on, a lovely period behaviour, and a green pool at the dock's foot. But indigo keys and chip banks fill the desk, so the light competes with navy, and some tubes carry thin data ('4 shown (up to 100)').
Lines ending in lamps carry 'now' well, but the tubes are at 0.8 and #74f0a3, so the halos are thinner than today's. This is the soul deficit its relit child fixes.
Its parent's light unchanged, so the same thin tubes. The larger 17px setting reads more comfortably, and the slashed Ø on the tubes is a nice terminal touch, but it adds no light.

The phosphor gets a home on every page, and To do's late-bar tube is real data. But the full-height column is mostly empty lit glass on Status, Plans and To do, a tall green wash rather than light where attention belongs. The paper 'here' block is the brightest thing that is not green.

There is true tube behaviour here: a warm-up from dark, a green bloom afterglow fading on cards, and an annunciator panel of lamps on Status. But violet plotting grids and all-caps mono nav pull toward 1969 hardware rather than the green tube, and the greeting's glass pool is weak.

It keeps the relit parent's light. The engraved pewter drawings are charming but not phosphor. Taking the icons out, and the 'Speak' text key, makes the bar read less like a machine, so the soul is unchanged or slightly less.

The monitors as lit exhibits under a picture light is a poetic answer to scarcity. The 404 and sign-in glow beautifully. But the greeting's glass pool is gone, and the single 22px size with brass tracked caps flattens the page around the one light.
A calm, legible listing, but the screens are at 0.81 and the glow at 0.9, so the tubes look dimmer than today's and nothing below the fold is lit.
The docked glass column is a good home for the light, but the tube is at 0.8, dead black sits under a short column, and indigo keys everywhere take the place of the glow.
The greeting is unlit, paper-grey cells are the brightest non-green, and the light is thin. The blueprint figures are well drawn but are not phosphor.

A handheld's LCD soul rather than a tube's. Four greens tint the ground and the olive card fills, so the page drifts back to green monochrome. Pixel fonts and chunky boxes are lively rather than calm, even though the phosphor display itself is kept.

fixes.suggestion: Keep: the white-hot now lamp with a breathing halo, the lit stretch of track from now to the next stop, the Status chain lit lamp to lamp, and tubes at 1.0 with spill. Fix: keep one breathing lamp per view on Home. Make To do's 'now' a steady lit tick (no breath) so the two do not pulse together. Carry the same rule where it is not yet seen: today on the Plans month as a lit lamp, the next setup step lit, and Settings' status lamp. Make the warm page-head rings dark glass with a 1px rim, not a bright lemon rim. The steel row afterglow reads as a selection, so make it a sage (#86d9a6) 10-12% wash fading over 1.2s. Consider letting Next up's tube draw the same fortnight as pulses, grafted from Long Persistence. Ship the one-line views.task_row late flag.

Keep the idea whole: the light is the data (the fortnight scope, due dates around NOW, the spend meter, NO SIGNAL on the 404), with chinned graphite cases and print everywhere else. Fix: lift the resting pulses to about 0.6 opacity with a 2px core so stills read. Put a 1px sweep core behind the text, never across it. Give the Plans month its own trace, a today stripe on a 4-week scope. Rebuild the Status legend tables as one-line rows with a leader to the state, as in Evening Listing, so 'The weekend digest' and 'Telegram bot token' stop wrapping in narrow columns. Keep the graticule sparse (4x3 is right) but add minor ticks on the axis.

Keep: the question typed on the glass under the blinking cursor, the tube warm-up from a line, the LED on the current key, numbered Contents with counts, and the terminal as Home's first screen. Fix: set VT323 only on glass and in the band's page-number tile. Band titles go in the sans at heading size, so VT323 stays the screen's voice. Cut the dither blocks behind titles to one small mosaic tile at the band's left. Deepen the case to a low-chroma brown-black (about #2a231d) so it reads as moulded plastic, not wood veneer. Put Coming up and To do side by side under the terminal to bring Home toward 2200px. Make the sticky key row the phone's tab bar only, not a second bar on desktop.

Bring one live light below the fold. Light Coming up's rail from the NOW lamp to the first stop (Track Relit's occupied track), and give To do's '2 late' a small amber ring lamp, not a glow. Make the row afterglow visible: a sage 10% wash with a 2px lit left edge fading over 1.2s. Put the date on the greeting back in VT323 so the glass keeps its terminal voice.

Keep the glass column and the To do late-bar tube. End the column at its content, make it sticky, and on idle pages fill it with one small data tube instead of empty lit glass. Paper for 'here' in the bar should drop a step (about #a9ab9f) so it is not the brightest non-green thing on the page.

Keep the picture light over each monitor and the monitors as the lit exhibits; it is the most elegant idea for scarcity. Put the greeting's glass pool back behind the question. Break the one-size rule at least for titles and the question (two steps). Set labels in sentence case, not brass tracked caps.

Keep the tube warm-up, the green afterglow bloom on cards, and the annunciator lamps. Let the annunciator replace the Status lists, not duplicate them. Set the nav in sentence case. Relight the greeting's pool under the question. Hold violet to thin plotting lines at low opacity so the green stays the only light.

Keep the NOW / NEXT / LATER spine with a lit NEXT lamp, and the phosphor display in its slate bezel. Return the ground to green-black and the card fills to slate, so green stays light rather than paint. Set headings in the sans; pixel type belongs on the screen only.

judges.notes: What I saw: the relit entrants this round all put back what the lens asks for. Their tubes run at exact #6dff9c with screenGlow 1.0, with bloom, scanlines, a chinned case and the greeting's green pool. The carried unlit parents (Evening Listing, Track Diagram, its Large Setting mutant, Docked Terminal) look visibly dimmer beside them at full size. What now separates the lit ones is whether the light reaches the rest of the page and means something there. Track Diagram Relit does this best: one rule (the now lamp and the lit track from it) lights Home below the fold, To do and Status, so the owner's 'reflect more of the page content' and 'bring the phosphor back' are answered by the same device. Long Persistence is the most original answer: the tubes draw the family's own weeks, due dates and spending, so the glow is information, not decoration. It needs brighter resting marks to survive a still. Videotex Sommaire has the most CRT heart (typing on the glass, a true warm-up, keys with LEDs), but it wears VT323 off the glass and grows Home to 3574px. Its terminal-as-Home idea is worth breeding into a calmer carrier. Evening Listing Relit is the best system, but its listing half is unlit. Grafting Track Relit's lit track onto its Coming up rail would close most of that gap. Motion worth keeping from the details strips: Videotex's and Flight Console's warm-up from dark or a line, Tuning Dock's roll bar, and Flight Console's green afterglow fading on a card, the closest to the kit's E-series afterglow. Afterglow is still invisible on the listing entrants (Evening Listing Relit, Long Persistence). Warnings: a full-height lit column (Blueprint Terminal) and a green-tinted ground (Pocket Timeline) both turn light into a wash. The owner's 'not a wash' applies to glass as much as to a corner.

scores.why: It has a real identity, the lit tube and the halo, but everything is green: glowing boxes, bubbles and pills, green on black at full contrast. That reads as the Matrix, not a family's evening page. It is the yardstick for the light this round is trying to bring back.
A calm, well-made programme listing, but the panel has seen this mood for rounds. The light is thin, the head column is empty on Ideas and To do, and the page is tasteful without being memorable.
The docked glass column is a strong idea. The raised indigo keys everywhere, including the tracked-caps ALL buttons, still read as Bootstrap navy, and the short column leaves dead black beneath it.
The signal box's lines carry order across Home, Chat and To do, which is a clear, exact mood. The light is dim on #74f0a3, and the slate and steel are now the default look of the pack.
The rule of lit against matte is clean and the tubes glow properly. The EFIS mono-caps labels and small tracked caps make it feel like an instrument panel dressed up, not a home.
Heads set into the rails and the halo returned to the key moments. The glowing bubble edges spread the light to things that are not live, and the look is close to its siblings.

The most rigorous conceit in the set: numbered chapters and a figure drawn from each page's data. It is let down by mono-caps chapter tabs, paper-grey cells that are the brightest thing on the page, and an unlit, brutal feel that is short on warmth.

The best-crafted of the listing family. The head columns now say how each band stands (4 open, 2 late), Chat hangs from a timetable rail, the tuning scale sits under the bar, and the halo is back on the greeting. It is refined rather than new, but it holds on every page.

The freshest answer to the owner's word. The phosphor is back doing a job: the scope traces the family's own weeks and due dates with a sweep and afterglow, and the rest of the page is quiet graphite print in true column-headed tables. It is compact, calm and memorable, with the light exactly where attention belongs.
A sensible written scale and larger type. At page scale it is almost indistinguishable from Track Diagram, and the slashed zero is invisible off the tubes.

The engraved pewter line drawings stand on Home's rules: hills and sun for Coming up, a clipboard, a jar of slips, a present with a wish, each with one thing in its section's colour. They add a bookish warmth no other entrant has. Away from Home, pages with the icons removed are plainer rather than richer, and the phone tabs lose recognition.

Better than its parent: the column now runs to a status line, the blueprint-grid tiles give a specific texture, and the To do tube with its late bars is lovely. The underlined periwinkle links everywhere feel like default web blue, and the paper 'here' block glares in the bar.

The most personality in the room. It is a family Game Boy, with a NOW/NEXT/LATER spine and a berry power light that kids would love. It is heavy-handed: pixel type on every item name, beveled cartridge boxes everywhere and an olive-green ground that makes the whole page greener, which works against the owner's calm.

A mature, original mood. The green screen hangs as an exhibit under a warm picture light, rooms are named on swallowtail banners, and brass and bone read in large print. It is elegant and grounded. The one-size rule flattens the hero: 'What's on your mind?' is no larger than body text, the extended tracked caps heads feel mannered, and Home runs long.

Witty and content-driven throughout. A console clock strip (TODAY, PLANS, LATE, HOLDS) heads Home, violet flight-plan arcs draw the coming weeks and the month, the setup steps count down T-3 to Go, a crew board of lamps sits on To do and a lamp panel on Status. Violet is a fresh companion with one job. The tiny mono-caps nav and the empty dotted tile columns are the weak spots.

The boldest return of the original tube. Home is the terminal itself, with the question typed on the green glass and a radar blooming above it, framed by warm brown plastic and a Minitel contents page. It is memorable and nostalgic. The pastel filled number tiles read as confetti, the VT323 double-height bands are costume on every page, and Home is 3574px long.

The console rule (keys that tune at the head, the lit answer at the foot) is a good idea, and the kind bank doubling as the legend helps. The indigo raised keys and the uppercase tracked keys still give it a generic dashboard feel, and the nine-key settings column is heavy.

Its best idea is that the lamp where you are now is lit and glows along the track from there. That gives Track Diagram's timetables a small, memorable story, and the lit title screens (lemon on To do, lilac on Ideas) add a touch of warmth. Beside its parent (6.8) the pages still look almost the same, in the same slate and steel-cyan as the other slate entries, so it reads as a careful refinement rather than a new mood. That puts it a notch above its parent but below Long Persistence (7.9) and Signal Legend, Drawn (7.2).

fixes.suggestion: Keep the scope as the page's one lit instrument and the column-headed graphite tables. The pulses are thin and faint at rest, so make them taller, with the next one labelled on the glass ('Pho Oregon') and a brighter afterglow. Put a month trace on Plans' month view, which today has no tube. On Home the second setup link turns amber on its own; keep amber to the numbered rings. On Status, give the WHAT column more room so 'Claude (Anthropic)' and 'The weekend digest' stop wrapping. Borrow Videotex's move and let the question's placeholder sit in the lit glass tone, so the greeting feels like the tube too.

Keep the clock strip and consider carrying a slim version on every page. Keep the flight-plan arcs, the T-minus setup steps, the crew board and the lamp panel, all good data-drawn graphics. Set the bar's places in sentence-case condensed sans at about 14px rather than tiny tracked mono caps, and do the same with 'ALL PLANS →' and 'ALL 4 →' as underlined sentence-case links. Collapse the empty dotted tile columns on the Kids' wishes and Lately added bays to a 56px lamp gutter, or put a small figure there. Give the grey bays a touch less box: one top rule rather than a full frame.

The craft is the benchmark. To make it memorable rather than merely right, give it one signature graphic. The tuning scale under the bar could become a real dial marking today, or Coming up's rail could carry Long Persistence's pulses. Let the NOW lamp glow as a breathing dot. Kind words mixed 72% toward the ink are the right call; keep them.

Make the drawings the system, not a Home ornament. Give each page head one (a calendar leaf with a ringed date for Plans, the clipboard for To do, the jar for Ideas, a lamp board for Status, a toolbox for Settings) and use them for empty states. Thicken the lines to about 1.75px so they read at 100%. Keep the icons on the phone tab bar for recognition. The desktop key squares are fine.

Keep the picture light over the monitor, the swallowtail room banners, brass labels and bone ink: the museum mood is the best new grounded palette of the round. Break the one-size rule once, for the question: a 34-40px display step for 'What's on your mind?' and page titles. Replace the extended tracked caps heads with small caps at .06em. Tighten Home by setting Coming up as one line per plan.

Keep the question typed on the glass and the radar blooming above it. It is the round's most faithful return of the original light and worth grafting elsewhere. Swap the pastel filled number tiles for outlined tiles or a coloured rule, so section colour lives in edges, not surfaces. Keep VT323 for the page title only, not every band head. Pull the brown plastic toward charcoal-umber, and collapse the long Coming up and To do rows to one line.

Keep the NOW/NEXT/LATER spine and the berry 'you are here' light, both good ideas for any design. Set item names and card titles in the sans, keeping pixel type only for page titles and stop labels. Return the ground to near-black rather than olive, and thin the bevels to one step, so the handheld frames the screen instead of covering the page.

Retune the links from periwinkle #94bbfe to a quieter blueprint #9fb4d6, and let the blueprint colour live mainly in the gridded tiles. Dim the paper 'here' block in the bar to a steel cap. The To do tube with its late bars is the best idea here; give every page's column foot a tube like it rather than empty glass.

judges.notes: Through the creativity and style lens, this round finally has new moods, not just new finishes. The entrants that answer the owner's 'bring some of that back' best are those whose light is the data, not those that raise the glow. Long Persistence's scope traces the family's own weeks with sweep and afterglow. Flight Console lights a lamp board and an arc of plans. Videotex types the question on the glass. The weaker relit mutants (Track Diagram Relit, Large Setting) are near-invisible changes at page scale. The graphic ideas worth breeding into the standard: data-drawn tubes (Long Persistence), a clock or readout strip and flight-plan arcs (Flight Console), engraved line drawings for the family's things (Signal Legend, Drawn), the question on the glass (Videotex), a picture light over the exhibit monitor (Night Gallery), and a NOW spine with one berry 'here' light (Pocket Timeline). Recurring faults to keep out: tiny tracked mono caps on navigation and 'see more' links (Flight Console, Figure Ground, Tuning Dock), pixel or display faces on item names (Pocket Timeline, Videotex bands), filled pastel tiles (Videotex), and one type size that flattens the hero (Night Gallery). A promising breed is Long Persistence's graphite tables and scope with Flight Console's clock strip and arcs, Signal Legend Drawn's engraved heads, and Evening Listing Relit's head-column summaries. Yardstick: today 4.4, best 7.9.

scores.why: Yardstick. A consistent card-and-pill kit, but green does every job (links, icons, edges, kinds): there is no colour code, no row drawing shared between pages, 45 of 57 small targets and a flat type scale. The light is lovely but spread across the whole page.

The most complete system on the panel. One band with a head column and one leader row to tabular facts, used on Home, Ideas, To do, Status and Settings. The head column now does a job on every page: count and state, the kind filter on Ideas, Open/Done on To do, List/Month on Plans. Steel reverse video means here, amber is only a ring, the Chat timetable ends in a lit ring at the box, and the tube is relit at 1.0 only on the phosphor list. Its faults are finish (duplicated head summaries, an invisible afterglow, facts far from their names on Status), not rules.

A new and very clear rule: each page has one lit instrument that draws its own data, and under it a print legend table with real column heads (DAY PLAN TIME IN, LAMP WHAT STATE, KIND IDEA FOR #). That is the best typesetting of lists this round and a real job for the phosphor. It loses ground on Status, whose three narrow tables wrap their names and states, on a heavy stacked To do filter box, and on a faint scope whose text sits on the sweep line.

Track Diagram's rule, lines only where there is order, now carries a lit now lamp into To do's due track, and the ring heads and status lamps glow. It is coherent and it holds on every page, but at page scale it is barely different from its parent. Ideas' tinted card grid and Status's boxed columns keep it box-heavy next to the listing.

Still an excellent listing system, but its own child does everything it does and more: a head column that says how each band stands, numbered rings, a Chat timetable and full tube light. Its empty head columns on Ideas and To do are now the visible gap.

The right move for a design system: five written steps instead of 29 sizes, with the name set as the body in 600 and never a size of its own. But the page it produces looks almost the same as Track Diagram, only longer. The single title step makes Sign in's title wrap, and kind labels at 13px sit next to 15px facts.
The lines-carry-order grammar is coherent and it reaches Chat, To do and setup. It is box-heavy on Ideas and Status, and the now light is dimmer than the relit sibling's.

Legends set into the rails, steel reverse video, square family surfaces against round glass. A clear state system with the light back on, but the setup tray is filled olive-bronze, the bubble edges glow on things that are not live, and Chat's times sit far from their bubbles.

A real system rule: every dock is a console, with the keys that choose what the desk shows at its head and the machine's answer on a tube at its foot. It pays off on Ideas (the kind bank works as filter and legend at once), To do and Plans, on a perfect-fourth scale. It fails on Home, where the dock is not sticky and leaves about 1000px of dead black, and it still uses tracked-caps keys (ALL PLANS, ADD AN IDEA) and navy-indigo starters.

The EFIS colour code and the lit-versus-matte rule are well argued. But heads and actions set as mono-caps legends in the demarcation lines rank below their rows, and the page reads as a code more than as a family's page.

Useful system pieces: a status foot on the machine's column on every page (READY, who answers, limit), sentence-case underlined blue links, amber kept to rings. But a blueprint tile heads every row and every head (about twenty identical squares), the paper here-block is the brightest non-green thing on the page, and the column is not sticky, so it leaves dead black under it or empty glass on Status and Plans.
The lit column is the right idea, but the indigo raised keys everywhere (five ALL keys on Home) read as Bootstrap navy, and the column ends in black. Its child Tuning Dock supersedes it.

The most information-dense new language. A readout strip (TODAY, PLANS, TO DO, LATE, IDEAS, HOLDS) gives the whole Home at a glance, and the drawings come from real data (flight plan, crew board, annunciator). Against it: all-caps nav and tracked-caps ALL links, an annunciator on Status that repeats the list under it, stops numbered 1 to 5 while the list starts at 2, a one-sided Chat log, 23 small targets and violet dot-grid noise.

The engraved line drawings are charming, but they are small, faint and found only on Home. Taking the icons out costs recognition in the nav and on the phone, where the wordmark is also hidden, and Speak text replaces the mic glyph. As a system this is a subtraction, and the olive setup fill remains.
The most rigorous numbering and figure rule, but it is square, cold and mono-caps: tracked caps buttons, text-only phone tabs, an unlit greeting and a paper-grey here-block.

It has the strongest identity and the best phosphor moment of the round: the question is typed on the lit tube itself, with a Contents list with counts and leaders beside it. The system underneath is heavy. VT323 double-height section titles are a fuzzy fourth voice, the brown plastic reads khaki, five pastel number tiles make confetti, rows are oversized (Home 3574px) and the sticky key row crosses the content.

Calm and large-print, and the picture light over each tube is a lovely way to say 'light where attention belongs'. But the one-size rule removes the greeting's hierarchy: the question is set at body size. Heads are tracked extended caps at about .2em, setup is a brown-filled tray, Chat is a one-sided log and the lit glass greeting is gone.

The NOW, NEXT and LATER spine is a strong structural rule that could run through every page. But the surfaces are moss and olive (green-family, so more monochrome, not less), pixel faces are set on card titles and page titles, and chunky double boxes wrap everything. It reads as a toy rather than the family's daily tool.

fixes.suggestion: Keep everything structural. (1) Drop head summaries that repeat the rows beside them: the kids' '0 open' over two '0 open' rows, and 'next in 2 days' echoing the first row's 'in 2 days'. Keep only counts that add something (4 open / 2 late, 12 ideas). (2) Ideas' kind key makes the head column nine cells tall: set it two-up (grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr) or fold it behind a disclosure below 72rem. (3) The afterglow does not show in the capture. Use a steel wash of about 10% with a 2px sage left edge, fading over 1.2s ease-out. (4) On Status and Settings, cap the row measure at about 62rem so a value is not 700px from its name. (5) Next up's tube stretches to the greeting's height and leaves empty glass: align-self:start, or graft Long Persistence's plan trace into the spare glass. (6) Give the steel a little more chroma (about #9cc4dc for the cap) so Chat is not 93% green. (7) Ship views.task_row `late` with the design.

Keep the rule (one instrument per page, a legend table under it, pointing at a row lights its mark) and the column-headed tables. (1) Status: give each group its own full-width table (or a single table with a Group column), because 'Claude (Anthropic)', 'Weather and travel' and the states wrap in the three narrow columns. (2) To do: set Show, Search and Filter on one row beside the scope instead of a stacked boxed panel. (3) Scope text: give NEXT UP and its lines their own band above the graticule so the sweep never crosses the words, and raise resting pulses from .3 to about .5. (4) A hovered setup link turns fully amber in the capture. Hover should go ink or steel, because amber means 'needs a look'. (5) Plans has no instrument; say why, or give it the month trace. (6) Move the Jinja date arithmetic and drive-text parsing into views.py.

The relighting does not show at page scale. Rather than carry it as a separate line, graft its one new part, the lit now marker dropped into To do's due track between late and upcoming, into Evening Listing, Relit's To do rows. Otherwise, replace Ideas' tinted card grid (the warm kinds read brown) with the listing row, and cut Status's boxed columns to rails.

Keep the console rule (keys at the head, the answer on a tube at the foot) and the kind bank as a filter and legend. (1) Make the dock sticky (position:sticky; top:<bar height>; max-height:calc(100vh - bar); overflow:auto), or end the desk mat level with it, so Home has no black under the dock. (2) Set 'All plans', 'All 4' and 'Add an idea' as sentence-case underlined links, never tracked-caps keys. (3) Make the starters slate keys, keeping indigo for the one latched key. (4) Raise the mono facts to about .8rem and pull them toward the title instead of pinning them far right.

Keep the question typed on the tube, the Contents list with dotted leaders to counts, and the power-on collapse. Fix the system under them. (1) Section titles in condensed Instrument Sans 600 at about 1.5rem; VT323 only inside glass. (2) One neutral straw tile for page numbers instead of five pastels, with the section colour only on a 3px cap. (3) Graphite case (#2c3135 to #44494f) instead of brown plastic. (4) Rows at a 1.05rem title with a single-line date tile, to bring Home under about 2400px. (5) Key row sticky on the phone only; on desktop it belongs in the bar. (6) Sentence case for the bar's Memory, Family and Status.

Keep the readout strip and make it the system's global element on every page, labels in sentence case and figures in Plex Mono. Keep the crew board as To do's figure. Remove the Status annunciator, which repeats the lamp list beneath it. Number the flight-plan stops to match the list (or put today's plan in the list). Restore icons and sentence case in the nav and on the ALL links, a two-sided Chat, 44px targets, and amber countdown lamps drawn as rings, not filled blocks.

Keep the picture light above each tube and the comfortable large-print body. Give the ask its own title step (the question must be the largest words on Home), replace the .2em extended-caps heads with condensed 600 sentence case, draw setup as an amber edge on slate rather than a brown fill, and bring back the two-sided Chat and the lit glass greeting.

Keep the NOW, NEXT and LATER spine as a rule for anything with a time. Move every surface off moss and olive onto the slate plastic already in the palette, keep pixel faces to the page title at most (never card or row titles), and thin the chunky double frames to one.

Keep the column's status foot and the underlined blue links. Put blueprint tiles on section heads only, not on every row. Take the paper here-block down to steel reverse video. Make the column sticky, or end it with its content.

Let the drawings coexist with the icons: restore the nav and phone-tab glyphs and the mic. Draw the pictures larger (about 48px) and use them as empty-state art on Plans, To do and Wishes, where they would earn their place. Draw setup as an amber edge, not a fill.

judges.notes: Through the system lens the round has a clear leader. Evening Listing, Relit is the first entrant whose head column has a job on every page (counts and state on Home, the kind filter on Ideas, Open/Done/Cancelled on To do, List/Month on Plans, on/off counts on Status). It solves round 10's biggest open problem and adds the timetable Chat every lens asked for, all within one row drawing, one here (steel reverse), one caution (amber rings) and a short lit list at full 1.0. Long Persistence is the most promising new rule: light as data (one instrument per page) over print legend tables with true column heads. Its table typesetting would improve any winner, and a breed of the two (the listing's head column and rows, Long Persistence's column heads and the plan trace in Next up's spare glass) is what I would write into the standard. Recurring system faults: tracked-caps controls and ALL links (Tuning Dock, Flight Console, Videotex, Night Gallery); one-sided Chat logs (Night Gallery, Flight Console); non-sticky docked columns that leave dead black (Tuning Dock, Blueprint Terminal); and amber or brown as a filled surface (Night Gallery, Signal Legend Drawn and Relit). The wild entrants changed the whole page, which the owner's test rewards, but each broke a rule that has held for rounds: one-size type flattening the greeting, a green-family ground, VT323 as a heading face, or pastel confetti tiles. Graft their ideas (the composer in the tube, the readout strip, the crew board, the picture light), not their grounds. Afterglow is invisible in almost every capture; whoever wins should make it visible at about 10% with a 1.2s fade.

scores.why: Yardstick. Blurred, Home shows several green blocks of equal weight, so the eye has no single path. 45 of 57 Home targets are under 44px. The desktop bar's right side is icons only, and the Send-where-I-am checkbox sits in the Tab order ahead of the mic and Send.

One-line rows read along a leader to tabular facts, with steel reverse for 'here' and 0 small targets on every page, and Home fits in 1640px. The head column is still dead space on Ideas and To do, and Next up has empty glass.

The machine column gives each page a clear place for what the machine says, and the phone composer is pinned above the tabs. The indigo keys everywhere (starters, the 'ALL' keys) all read as primary actions and blur which one matters.
The lines carry order: the now lamp, the setup track and the timetable To do all read at a glance. There is one small target on every page, and the Chat times sit in a far gutter.
Lit against matte makes the live things easy to find. The caps legends and the faceplate density make the heads rank close to their rows, so the lists take longer to scan.
Steel reverse for 'here' and one lit lamp per page give clear state. The trays and rail legends are tidy, but on Home the rows and heads are near one weight when squinted.

Numbered chapters and figures are rigorous and late tasks are marked. But there are 14 small targets on Home and 20 on To do, the buttons are mono caps, the phone tabs are text only, and Home is 2437px long.

The best-working page. Every head column now says how its band stands ('4 open / 2 late', 'next in 2 days') and does a job: one-click kind filters on Ideas and an Open/Done/All switch on To do. The rows are one line to tabular facts, and a NOW lamp starts the Coming up rail. Blurred, the order runs question, then Send, then the lit tube, then rows. It has 0 small targets on every page and a Chat with the date once and each time at its bubble.

The column heads (DAY PLAN TIME IN, TASK WHO DUE, LAMP WHAT STATE) make every list and Status say what each fact is. Home in two columns is the shortest (1634px), To do's scope shows late at a glance, pointing at a row lights its mark on the tube, and the Tab order matches the drawing. It loses a little on the phone, where the scope's trace crowds the Next up words.
The larger 17px setting on a five-step scale reads more easily for a family, and the track keeps its order cues. The pages are longer, titles wrap on the phone, and one small target remains.

Words in the desktop bar and the labelled 'Speak' button say exactly what they do, and the setup drawings make each step easy to recognise. On the phone, tabs with words only under a faint 3px cap lose the icon recognition, and the drawings on each head are decoration the eye has to pass.

One rule that holds on every page: the machine's column (ask, Next up, a READY/limit status line with a Status link) and the family's desk. The phone Chat composer is pinned above the tabs, the Tab order matches the drawing, and there are 0 small targets. The column does not stick, so Home scrolls into black under it, and the paper 'here' block is the brightest thing that is not green.

The lit now lamps and occupied track make 'what is next' readable at a glance on Home, To do and Chat, and the family's plates stay calm. One small target remains, and the Ideas cards are a slower read than a list.

The NOW / NEXT / LATER spine is a strong way to tell time at a glance. But the pixel faces on heads and titles slow reading and wrap, there are 7 small targets on Home and 25 on To do, and the berry 'was due' reads as an alarm.

The large print is easy to read and the setup panel is clear. With one type size, hierarchy is gone when squinted, the heads are tracked caps, Chat drops the split between mine and hers, there are 20 small targets on Home, and Home is 2346px long.

The readout strip at the top of Home (TODAY, PLANS 05, LATE 02, HOLDS 03) is the best glance summary of the round, but it is not clickable. The nav is small tracked caps, there are 23 small targets on Home, Chat is one-sided, and the kids' wishes sit above Coming up.

The numbered Contents on Home, with counts and anchor links, tells you what the page holds in one look. But the main nav moves to a sticky key row at the foot on the desktop, last in the Tab order. There are 35 of 62 small targets on Home, Home is 3574px long with setup at the very bottom, and the ask box reads as tube text rather than a field.

The rule is easy to learn: every page's controls sit in the dock (Kind, For, Show and View as latched one-tap keys) with the machine's answer on a tube at its foot. It has 0 small targets, and the phone Chat composer is pinned. On the phone, Ideas spends about 360px on the console before its title, and the indigo starters compete with Send as actions.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the working head column, the one-line rows and the NOW rail. Now that the head column's kind list filters Ideas, drop the Kind select from the form so there is one kind control, not two. Make the head-column states links ('2 late' goes to To do filtered to late, 'next in 2 days' to Plans). Remove summaries that repeat what is beside them ('0 open' above two '0 open' rows). Let the Next up tube end with its words, or enlarge the radar, so no empty glass is left. Hold the leaders to about 60rem so the eye does not travel 500px of dots to reach the facts.

Keep the column-headed tables on Home, To do and Status, the data-drawn scope, and the hover that lights a row's mark. Under about 40rem, put the trace below the Next up words (or hide the pulses) so they no longer overprint the date. Confine the sweep beam to the plot area under the text. Replace the 40 per-row CSS keys with a data attribute so any number of rows light. Let the To do WHO and DUE columns take fixed widths so 'Book the campsite at Silver Falls' holds one line. Keep the word 'radar', or say 'chart', rather than 'scope'.

Keep the rule (controls in the dock, the answer on its tube) and the latched one-tap Kind, For and Show keys. On the phone, put the page title first and fold the console behind a single 'Filter' disclosure so the list is not pushed 360px down. Turn the starters to slate so indigo marks only Filter and the page's own action and Send stays the one lit primary. Lighten the nine joined settings keys to a list with a reverse block for 'here'.

Make the machine column sticky (position:sticky; top:1rem; max-height:calc(100vh - 2rem)), with the status line always at its foot, so a reader who scrolls keeps the glass. Dim the paper 'here' block in the bar a step toward steel so it stops being the brightest thing that is not green. Keep blueprint tiles on the section heads only, and give rows their kind square alone, to cut the per-row noise.

Keep the numbered Contents with counts and anchor links, which is the round's best 'what is on this page' device, and the pinned phone composer. Put the main places back in the top bar on the desktop (a key row can stay as the phone's tab bar). Bring Finish setting up to the top of the Contents while it has steps. Draw the ask as a bounded field with a focus ring inside the tube rather than as tube text. Raise the keys and the Contents rows to 44px. Tighten the section spacing to bring Home from 3574px nearer to 2000px.

Keep the readout strip and make each cell a 44px link (PLANS to Plans, LATE to To do filtered to late, HOLDS to setup). Set the nav in sentence case at text size rather than small tracked mono caps. Restore the family-on-the-right split in Chat. Put Coming up before the kids' wishes. Keep the violet figures only where they add something the words do not (the Coming up track).

Put the icons back on the phone tab bar (keep the coloured cap as a legend). Keep the words in the desktop bar and the labelled 'Speak'. Keep the setup drawings, which help recognition, but take the drawings off the section heads so the rule reads as a rule.

Keep the large 18-20px body for the family, but add one heading step so hierarchy survives the squint. Set the section heads in sentence case rather than tracked caps, restore the Chat bubbles with the family on the right, and raise the 20 small Home targets to 44px.

Keep the NOW / NEXT / LATER spine on Home. Set titles and heads in a readable sans (pixel face only for the NOW stamp and the tab icons), use amber rather than berry for 'was due', and raise the To do ticks and edit links to 44px.

judges.notes: Through this lens the round's clear gain is structural. The informed entrants now answer "what is this page and how does it stand" before any row is read: head columns that state counts and late (Evening Listing, Relit), column heads that name every fact (Long Persistence), a dock that always holds the page's controls (Tuning Dock), and a status line in the machine column (Blueprint Terminal). All four have 0 small targets on every page and a Tab order that matches the drawing. The best score here is 8.4 against 4.0 for today's page. For the standard, I would write in: (1) every list names its facts, either by a head column or by column heads; (2) a filter that is one tap (kind keys or links) beats a select plus a Filter button, and the page should keep one control per filter, not both; (3) on the phone, the Chat composer is pinned above the tab bar (Blueprint Terminal, Tuning Dock, Videotex); (4) one glance summary at the top of Home (Flight Console's readouts, Videotex's Contents), made of links. What the wild entrants still lose on is the same as before: small targets (20-35 on Home), tracked caps for nav and heads, one-sided Chat, and very long Home pages. What they add worth grafting is the glance summary. The light came back without hurting comprehension: in the squint the lit tube and Send lead the eye in the informed and relit entrants, and nothing else competes.

scores.why: Today's page (DM Sans, DM Mono, VT323 on the tubes) has no written scale. Its facts are loose prose lines with small 'in 3 days' pills, headings are barely larger than the rows, and nothing lines up down a column. It reads fine but is not typeset.

Evening Listing typeset one step further. The head column now carries a figure: a large '12' over IDEAS and '4 / OPEN / 2 late' on To do, which fixes the empty-column problem with type rather than filler. Setup steps are numbered rings, and rows keep one line with leaders into tabular date, time and relative sub-columns. The weak spots are the lowercase-mono summaries ('4 more' of what?) and 'Edit, complete, or snooze' set bold on every To do row.

The best new typesetting idea this round: every list becomes a true table with a small caps header row (DAY PLAN TIME IN, TASK WHO DUE, KIND IDEA DRIVE WAY FOR #, PART / HOW IT STANDS). Times and drives are right-aligned in Plex Mono with slashed zeros, under condensed Archivo heads, and it holds on Home, Ideas, To do and Settings. It falls down on Status: three narrow three-column tables wrap states to three or four lines, and 'LAMP' as a column head is jargon. On Home, 'Book the campsite at / Silver Falls' wraps needlessly.

Still an excellent listing system: condensed Instrument Sans heads, one-line rows along dotted leaders, and Plex Mono tabular facts in fixed sub-columns. Its relit child does everything it does, and its head column is still empty on Ideas and To do.

A real type mutation. Body is 17px at 1.6 and the scale has five written steps (48/24 over 17/15/13), with labels one step larger and less tracked. Chat and Status read noticeably more comfortably than in the parent. But Ideas are still prose cards, where the larger size causes extra wraps ('south-east of / home'), and 'DUE' collides with '4 shown (up to 100).' on one line.

Good timetable setting: times hung in a mono margin, condensed Archivo heads and tabular times on the track. Ideas and Status facts are still prose ('about 27 min south of home (estimate)'), and the body is a size smaller than its Large Setting mutant.
The same typesetting as Track Diagram. The lit 'now' in the To do margin is a light, not a type change, so it scores the same as its parent through this lens.

A console with a real type system: Plex Sans Condensed heads, zero-padded tabular readouts (PLANS 05, LATE 02) across Home's top, FIG captions in Plex Mono, and a chat typeset as a flight log (speaker in caps, mono stamp, words below), which is elegant. Against it: tracked caps on nav, buttons and links ('ADD AN IDEA', 'ALL PLANS', 'FILTER'), and widows ('switched / off', 'setup / page').

Taking the icons out lets type carry the page: word-only nav, #1 to #4 designators, a masthead with title and deck on one line, and IBM Plex Sans with Plex Mono throughout. It feels bookish. But the deck is top-aligned rather than on the title's baseline, the facts are middot prose with no column, the stacked mono-caps 'WAS DUE / 2 DAYS AGO' is loud, and the drawings push each head off its rule rhythm.

A sound Plex superfamily with heads set into the rules and a mono due margin. The facts are prose and the stacked mono caps in the margin are heavy. Structurally close to its Drawn mutant, minus the numerals.

Plex Sans with Martian Mono, and a nice mono eyebrow over each name ('THURSDAY 1 OCTOBER, 10:00' above 'Silver Falls hike'). But section heads are tracked mono caps (COMING UP, TO DO), which rank weakly above 400-weight names, and 'was due / 2 days ago' breaks over two lines.

A coherent manual. Numbered sections (1.2, 1.3) sit in the heads, FIG captions label the figures, and a large 48px question gives a clear top. But nav, links and buttons are tracked mono caps ('ALL PLANS', '01 HOME'), and Home is long.
Condensed Archivo heads are strong, but the small text drops to about 12px ('Thursday 1 October, 10:00'), the relative facts are tiny mono, and 'ALL PLANS' and 'ADD AN IDEA' are uppercase keys.

A perfect-fourth scale is a good idea, but its low steps are too small. Facts and model names fall to about 11-12px (mono 'OpenAI, gpt-6-luna', 'nowhere else to go…'), and the kind words and keys are tracked extended caps (ACTIVITY, ALL IDEAS, ANY). The italic footer tagline is a nice touch.

Sentence-case underlined links are an improvement on Docked Terminal. But Status sets whole sentences in right-aligned mono ('nowhere else to go: one key, or the fallback is switched off'), and the setup tray's three narrow columns wrap to three lines while their summary floats top-right. The facts are tiny.

Some lovely typographic devices: a numbered Contents list with dotted leaders to its figures, page-number tiles, and double-height VT323 titles that bring the tube's voice to each band. But VT323 off the tube at 28-40px reads coarse, item names in 700 weight with underlines shout, the nav is mono caps, and Home runs to 3574px.

The bold single-size rule gives large-print calm and two fine things: a playscript chat (speaker and stamp in a column, words beside) and wall-label pairs on Status. But the page title is gone from the reading line (it survives only in a rotated banner), the question is no larger than the body, section heads are extended caps at wide tracking, and the legal line is set at 22px, so there is no hierarchy to scan.

The pixel faces carry personality but cost legibility. Idea names in Pixelify at 20px wrap ('Oaks Park / roller rink'), Silkscreen's wide caps ('IN 10 DAYS') are loud, and rounded Nunito body pulls toward a toy rather than the phosphor.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the head-column figure and make it the rule on every band: a large tabular numeral with a small caps label under it ('4 PLANS / next in 2 days', '12 IDEAS', '3 ON / 1 OFF'). Drop the lowercase-mono sentences, and say what '4 more' counts. On To do, make 'Edit, complete, or snooze' a quiet regular-weight link or a pencil at the row's end, not bold on every row. Borrow one header row per band from Long Persistence (WHO, DUE) where the facts are unlabelled, and set the weekday-date sub-column in tabular figures so '1', '4', '9' and '17 October' align on the digit.

Keep the tables, the right-aligned tabular mono figures and the header rows; this is the typeset system worth writing into the standard. Fix Status: either give each band a full-width two-column table (WHAT | STATE) with the lamp inside the WHAT cell, dropping the 'LAMP' head, or stack the three tables. Every state should hold one line. On Home's To do, narrow WHO and let TASK take the slack so 'Book the campsite at Silver Falls' holds one line. Balance decks with text-wrap: balance (To do's 'mean to / get done.'), and align checkboxes to the first line's baseline.

The 17px/1.6 body and the five-step written scale should breed into the leaders. Apply it to a one-line Ideas row with a tabular drive column instead of prose cards, so the larger size stops causing wraps. Give 'DUE' and '4 shown (up to 100).' separate lines, and raise the kind words from 13px to the 15px step so no label sits smaller than the text beside it.
Superseded by its relit child in this lens. If it is carried again, fill the head column with the figure and count as the child does.

Keep the flight-log chat, the zero-padded readout row and the FIG captions: the strongest console typography yet. Move nav, buttons and 'see more' links to sentence case, keeping tracked caps only for eyebrows, annunciator legends and speakers. Set body in Plex Sans (regular width) and keep Condensed for heads, then add text-wrap: pretty to remove the widows.

Keep the numbered Contents with leaders to right-aligned figures and the page-number tiles; they are true pagination typography. Set VT323 only on the glass and the tiles, and put band titles in a condensed sans at the head step. Drop item names from 700 to 600 with underline only on hover, set the nav in sentence case, and tighten the per-band spacing so Home is not 3.5k px.

Keep the playscript chat and the wall-label pairs (bold name, regular state). Add back two steps: a title step of about 2x for the page title (horizontal, in the reading line) and for 'What's on your mind?', and a small step for the legal line and captions. Cut the extended caps tracking from about .2em to .06-.08em.

Insert a 15px step between the 17px body and the 12px floor so facts and model names are not at the floor. Set the kind words and keys in sentence case at normal width; the colour key already carries the legend.

Set the masthead deck on the title's baseline rather than top-aligned. Put the facts in a right-hand tabular column instead of middot prose, and set the due margin in sentence-case mono ('was due 2 days ago') rather than stacked caps.

Keep Pixelify for page titles and the NOW / NEXT / LATER stop labels only. Set item names in the body face, reduce Silkscreen's tracking, and replace Nunito with a straighter sans so the pixel voice is an accent, not the reading face.

judges.notes: Through this lens the listing family still leads. Evening Listing, Relit is the most finished typesetting on the panel, and its head-column figures ('12 IDEAS', '4 OPEN / 2 late') fix last round's empty column with type. Long Persistence is a whisker behind, but it brings the one genuinely new typographic device: tables with header rows and right-aligned tabular figures, the same on Home, Ideas, To do and Settings. Its Status page is the only thing holding it back (narrow three-column tables that wrap). The breed to try is Evening Listing's one-line bands and leaders, with Long Persistence's header row once per band where facts are unlabelled, Track Diagram Large Setting's 17px/1.6 body and five-step written scale, and Flight Console's flight-log chat. Every entrant that uses tracked or extended caps on controls or links (Flight Console, Tuning Dock, Docked Terminal, Figure Ground, Night Gallery, Videotex) loses points again; keep caps to eyebrows, legends and speakers. The wild entrants each have one device worth grafting: Videotex's numbered Contents with leaders, Night Gallery's playscript chat, and Flight Console's zero-padded readout row. Pixel faces (Pocket Timeline) and VT323 off the glass (Videotex) cost legibility. Every candidate differs from today's page well beyond the greeting's corner, so the owner's 'nearly identical' concern no longer separates them. Today scores 5.4 and the best this round 8.3.

scores.why: The easiest to use in the round. Each head column now shows how its band stands (4 open, 2 late; 12 ideas; 4 more, next in 2 days), so Home can be taken in at a glance. On Ideas, All ideas, Restaurants and every kind are one click in the head column. To do gets Open, Done, Cancelled and All as a nav, with 'was due 2 days ago' in amber and amber tick-wells, so overdue shows on both Home and the page. judges.notes:
I walked each candidate's own pages through the family's tasks.

- **Send Vera a message and read the reply.** Every candidate works. Night Gallery reads best at night. Docked Terminal, Blueprint Terminal and Tuning Dock pin the composer on the phone, but on desktop it sits away from where the thread ends. Videotex's in-tube field reads as display text, not a field.
- **See what is on this weekend.** Every candidate works. Flight Console's readout strip and Evening Listing, Relit's head-column summaries are the fastest glance.
- **Show only the restaurants.** One click almost everywhere. Evening Listing, Relit and Tuning Dock also make every kind one click.
- **Tick off a to-do and see what is overdue.** This is the task that separates the field. Only Evening Listing, Relit, Long Persistence, Blueprint Terminal, Tuning Dock, Figure Ground and Flight Console mark late on the To do page itself. Track Diagram Relit shows it by colour and position only, having dropped the words. Every other candidate needs the one-line views.task_row `late` flag.
- **Find a date on Plans.** Works everywhere except Pocket Timeline, whose month grid shrinks to a small tube.
- **Change a setting.** Words in the bar (Evening Listing, Relit; Long Persistence; Tuning Dock; Signal Legend, Drawn; Docked Terminal; Blueprint Terminal) make Settings, Status, Family and Memory findable at first sight, which icons alone do not.
- **Sign in.** Fine in all.

Targets under 44px on Home: 0 in the listing and dock families, 1 on the track family, and 7 to 35 on the wild entrants (Videotex 35, Flight Console 23, Night Gallery 20). No page overflows. The smallest text is 12px or more on most; Large Setting is 13 and Night Gallery 22.

Losses:
- Night Gallery's sideways page titles.
- Videotex moving the main nav to a key row under the terminal and setup to the last section.
- Pocket Timeline's pixel item names.
- Track Diagram Relit dropping the 'was due' words from its To do page.

On the owner's test, every candidate changes the page well beyond the corner, and the relit ones put the light on the live things, which helps attention rather than hurting it. The one exception is Long Persistence's sweep line crossing the Next up words.

The standard a usability judge would write:
1. The bar names every place in words.
2. Each band's head says how it stands (counts, late).
3. Late is amber words on both Home and To do, never colour alone.
4. A filter is one click and behaves the same way everywhere.
5. Controls and see-more links are sentence case.
6. No target is under 44px.
7. Phosphor light is kept for the live list.

Today's page scores 5.0; the best this round, Evening Listing, Relit, scores 8.8.

designs.name: Track Diagram, Large Setting
designs.tagline: Track Diagram reset in a larger, more generous type: 17px body at 1.6, two heading steps over three text steps, labels a step larger and less tracked, and slashed zeros on the machine's figures.
designs.concept: This is Track Diagram with only the type changed. The steel-cyan lines on green-black slate, the lamps and the timetable margins are all kept. The type is larger (17px body at 1.6) and uses a written scale of five steps where the parent had twenty-nine sizes. A thing's name is the body set in 600, never a size of its own. That leaves two heading steps (24px heads, 48px titles) over three text steps (13px labels, 15px small text and controls, 17px body), with an 18px lede under each title. Labels are a step larger and a step less tracked, and the machine's figures draw a slashed zero, which now shows on the tubes in 4Ø4, 17:ØØ and 1Ø places.
designs.companions: Unchanged from the parent. Steel-cyan #a7c4d8, fixed as --steel, is the one companion: links, rings, 'here' in the bar and the tab bar, tab caps, the Settings nav, today on the month, and the family's avatars and bubble bar. Green-black slate (#0f1519 boards, #161c20 plates) carries every page. Cobalt #4f66e0 lights the greeting's top-right corner. The section and kind colours appear only in lamps, icons and tints.
decisions: I wrote the scale into :root as tokens: --t-label 13px, --t-small 15px, --t-body 17px, --t-lede 18px, --t-head 24px and --t-title clamp(2.4rem, 4.4vw, 3rem). Every size the parent and the base sheet set now sits on one of these steps, including Plans, To do, Settings, setup, Wishes and the forms. I ran a type audit of fifteen pages at 1280px and 390px. It went from 29 distinct text sizes to 10. Four of the ten are not on the scale: the phone's title clamp, the two FamilyDB word marks, and one inline-code case.

Fewer, clearer heading steps. Page titles, Sign in, the 404 and the setup pages share one 48px title; the parent used 48.8, 41.6, 36.8, 33.6 and 30.4. Every head is 24px Archivo 650, where the parent used 27.2, 25.6, 22.7 and 19.2. That covers section heads, panel heads, the month, the kids' conversations and the greeting's question, which stays in DM Sans. Names of things are the 17px body at weight 600: plate titles, idea cards, To do tasks, Status lights, Settings cards, Vera's name and the restaurants link. That step is marked by weight, not by size.

A fold that opens a form is a control, so it is set at the name step (17px DM Sans 600). This covers 'Put something on the calendar', 'Plan it', 'Record how it went' and 'Tell Vera something', and matches the parent's own 'Add something to do' and 'Save a thought for later'. A fold of settings (.fold) keeps the head step, like the panel heads beside it. This is the one place the new steps changed how something is drawn and not only its size.

Labels are one step larger and one step less tracked. Mono stamps, the DUE legend, eyebrows, weekday heads, said-by lines, ids, counts, dates and tags go from 11.2-12.8px to 13px. Caps tracking goes from 0.05em to 0.03em. Said-by lines, relative dates and the footer go from 0.02em to 0.01em. Small text goes from 13.6-14.7px to 15px: when, facts, hints, field labels, buttons, tabs, the bar, starters and section links. The smallest text on every page is now 13px, against 11.5px today.

On the tubes the change reaches only the legends and the small words. NEXT UP, ON THE RADAR and SPENT TODAY go from 1.2-1.25rem to 1.3-1.35rem, and tube caps tracking from 0.08em to 0.05em. The radar note on Ideas goes from 1.15rem to 1.25rem, and the 404 readout from 1.3rem to 1.4rem. The large tube figures keep the parent's sizes.

Slashed zero. DM Mono's normal zero is already slashed and the font has no 'zero' feature, so on the page's stamps only the declaration changes. VT323 does have the feature, and every tube now draws it: 4Ø4 and CONTACTS Ø on the 404 page, 17:ØØ on Next up, 1Ø places on the radar, and the spend readout. It suits the period, since terminals then slashed the zero. The shipped VT323 (static/fonts/vt323.woff2) lacks the feature, so the library's full copy would have to ship. The kids' '0 open' counts stay in DM Sans, as the parent chose.

The larger type needed some layout changes: (1) Home's To do margin is 0.6rem wider (7.6rem) so 'in 2 days 19:56' at 13px clears its lamp. (2) On the phone, Coming up's margin is 5rem instead of 4.1rem, with its relative dates untracked; at 4.1rem 'in 10 days' already overflowed the board in the parent. (3) The column gap in Home's ask row goes from 0.75rem to 0.5rem so Send stays last on the From row; at first it wrapped to its own line. (4) The lamps on Status (1.3rem to 1.4rem) and on the To do page (1.55rem to 1.72rem) move down to the middle of the taller names. (5) Sign in's ring and rail now start at the first line of its title.

Type tuning: when a fact wraps, such as an idea card's 'about 21 min south-east of home', its icon stays with the first line instead of floating between the two. Code inside a command block takes the block's 15px.

One markup change, in ideas.html: the radar's note ties each figure to its unit with a no-break space ('15 min', '45 min', '2 h'). At the larger tube size it had broken as 'and 2 / h by road'. Nothing else in the parent's templates changed, and no words changed.

Where I bent the roll: it asked for a 17-18px body. I set 17px, and used 18px only for the lede and long descriptions. At 18px the Coming up plates and Home's dashboard names wrap, and Home would grow far more than 19px. Sign in's title follows the single title step, so it now sets in two balanced lines ('Sign in / to FamilyDB'). Keeping it on one line would have meant widening the form column by about 7rem.
designs.measures: Full render: 0 hard checks failed. One guideline missed, the parent's own: Home's words differ from today's by 4.4% (the clock and the timetable legend). ink_on_bg 12.75, brand_on_bg 15.18; brand #6dff9c exact, screen #74f0a3. Green share of colour: Home 53.7%, Ideas 62.2%, Chat 70.7%, Status 32.6%. Hue entropy: Home .545, Ideas .489, Chat .407, Status .397. Kinds CIEDE2000 typical/deutan/protan 13.6 / 5.5 / 7.4; sections 12.8 / 5.5 / 5.3. Greeting corner pixel (1150,120) = (25,34,47), the same as the parent. Smallest text 13px on every page (today 11.5px). No sideways scroll anywhere. One target under 44px per page (the skip link), as in the parent. Home is 1769px tall (parent 1750). The type audit finds 10 distinct text sizes (parent 29): 13, 15, 17, 18, 24 and 48, plus the 38.4px phone title, the two FamilyDB marks and inline code. CSS is 57,337 characters.
strengths: A written, visible type system: five steps plus a lede, stated as tokens and carried to every page, so anyone can name the size of anything on the site. This is principle 21 of the standard carried through the whole site.

The page reads larger and calmer without the design changing: 17px body at 1.6 in the chat and on every plate, labels at 13px everywhere (smallest text up from 11.5px), and names set apart by weight rather than by another size.
Heads are clearer: one 24px head and one 48px title across the site, so the same kind of head is always the same size. Folds that open a form are set as controls and folds of settings as heads.
The slashed zero appears where it means something, on the green screens, and reads as a real terminal's figure.

Everything the parent won is kept: lines only where there is order, lamps at every stop, steel-cyan for the family's hand, slate on every page, one small target per page, no sideways scroll, and the greeting's cobalt corner (25,34,47).

designs.concept: This is Signal Legend Relit with the pictogram layer taken out. Each section is now named by a word and a coloured legend key. Each list row starts with a numeral or a letter, and the "here" state is the steel reverse block. The bar and the rows read as set type, the way a signal box's printed legend does. The one place for pictures is Home. There, each section head has a small engraved line drawing standing on the head's rule, as if the rule were the ground: the sun coming up over hills for Coming up, a clipboard and pencil for To do, a wrapped present with a wish rising for the kids' wishes, and a jar of idea slips for Lately added. The setup steps have drawings in the same hand. The intended feel is calmer and more bookish than an app full of icons, with some warmth where the family's own things are.
designs.companions: No new colours. The companions are the parent's (steel #a7c4d8 links and the reverse block, cream #ebe6da heads, slate trays), and each now has one more job. The section colours act as a legend. A 7px key square sits before each place in the desktop bar: steel for Vera, lilac #b58cec for Ideas, cyan #70dcf4 for Plans, lemon #f7dc78 for To do, pink #ff9fd0 for Wishes. On the phone the key is a 3px cap over each tab word, at 45% for the other tabs and full strength for the current one. Each drawing is in pewter-steel #8e99a6 with exactly one thing in its section's colour: the sun in cyan, the pencil in lemon, the wish sparkles in pink, the pulled-out idea slip in lilac. In the setup panel the one thing is amber #ffb850 (the key, the message bubble, the ringed date, the lit window, your mug's stripes, the kids' mugs), because amber keeps its one job, "needs a look". Idea numerals take the kind colour on the parent's kind-tinted designator. Kids' initials are pink on the pink-tinted designator. Settings numerals are steel, with the one that needs a look in amber. The #6dff9c signature and all of the parent's light are untouched: the lit mark, the caret, "mind", Send, the now lamp and the monitors.
decisions: Rolled major change, no icons at all. The system is the icon macro, not a CSS hide: in variants/r11-mut-2/templates/_ui.html, icon() returns nothing (a label becomes screen-reader text) and kind_icon() is empty. So every template, including the ones the parent never overrode, gets words only. The masthead's title tile is gone, and the h1 stands alone over its Oxford rule, which is already led in the page's colour. The tick is drawn in CSS. The done and cancelled task boxes draw a CSS tick and dash. base.html drops dictate.js's data-icons, so the mic carries the word 'Speak'. A safety rule hides any .icon a script might still inject.

Kept exactly one picture: the page's own mark (the logo, also the favicon), through a new mark() macro, in the bar and the foot. The owner's direction lists 'the mark' among the bright green signature places, and the tile is the bar's lit logo, not a pictogram for a function. I say this openly because a strict reading of the roll would remove it too.

Where an icon stood alone, a numeral, letter or coloured mark replaces it. Idea rows (Home's Lately added, the Ideas list, Status's waiting lookups) start with the idea's number '#7' in mono, in the kind colour. The number moves out of the facts column, which is set to 0 so the title gets the width. Kids' rows start with the kid's initial in pink. The nine Settings cards are numbered 1-9 as a table of contents, and Personality's glyph screen also gives way to its number there. Memory and Recent-activity rows get a square key, amber-filled for a firm memory. Empty rows get an em dash. Idea meta items are separated by a middle dot in place of the car and person pictograms.

Bar: the places are words with a section-colour key square before each. The tools (Memory, Family, Status, Settings) now show their words at every width instead of four pictograms. The key's colour is fixed to var(--link) for Home and Vera, so it does not follow the page accent: on To do it had turned lemon. On the phone the tab bar is words at .84rem with a coloured cap. Its current tab keeps the parent's here-cell fill and gets a full-strength 2rem cap. The phone's top bar hides the 'FamilyDB' wordmark visually (it stays the link's accessible name) so the four tool words fit, leaving the lit mark and caret.

The ask box: Send shows its word at every width. On the phone the bar reflows to 'From [who is asking?] [Send]' over 'Send where I am ... [Speak]', so the select is not squeezed. The mic in other fields is a 'Speak' word in the link colour.

Rolled minor change, line drawings. One sprite of real assets, variants/r11-mut-2/static/sketches.svg: 11 symbols in one hand, placed through a sketch() macro that uses <use>. Colour comes from the page through inheritance: color is the line, stroke is the one accent, and fill is the ground colour, so front shapes hide back ones (the hill hides the sun's lower half, the jar hides the slip, the roof hides the chimney). There is no style element and no text. Head drawings are drawn 72x40 and shown at 90x50 with 1.3 strokes, which come out at about 1.6px. Setup drawings are 56x36 at 1:1 with 1.5 strokes.

The head drawings stand ON the parent's double rail.
