Setup: Home's panel replaces the amber ring markers with a drawing per step on a short amber rule (password: an open lock and its key; Telegram: a phone and a message bubble, not the brand's paper plane; Calendar: a desk calendar with one day ringed). designs.name: Track Diagram Relit
designs.tagline: Track Diagram with the tube switched back on: the same steel lines on slate boards, and everything the diagram marks as live (the now lamp, the status lamps, her screens, the monitors, the ring where it is your turn) glowing and breathing like phosphor again.
designs.concept: This is Track Diagram with its tube switched back on. The signal box's diagram is kept whole: steel lines on green-black slate boards, a lamp at every stop, and times in a timetable margin. Everything it marks as the machine's, or as live, gives off light again the way the original green screen did. The monitors bloom and spill onto the page, her screens glow and pool light into her bubbles, and live lamps are white-hot points in a breathing phosphor halo. One rule carries the light through every page: the lamp where you are now is lit, and the section of track it stands on is lit from it, fading toward the next stop. The slate, the steel and the family's plates stay matte, so the page is calm and the light falls only where something is live.
designs.companions: Unchanged from Track Diagram. Steel-cyan #a7c4d8 is the family's hand: links, 'here', rings, tab caps and today on the month. Green-black slate carries the trays and plates (#0f1519 boards, #161c20 plates on #262e35 edges, a #0f1519 bar). Headings are cream #ebe6da and labels a quiet steel #a3b3bf. The section and kind colours live in their lamps, icons and tints. A cobalt wash, #4f66e0 at 2.4, sits in the greeting's top-right corner (sampled (24,34,46)). One role changes: each page's terminus ring is a small lit screen in its page's colour, as the original title tile was. That is steel on Home, Vera, Status and Settings. On Ideas and Plans it is lilac and cyan glass inside a rim of the same colour. On the warm pages (To do, Wishes, Family, Memory) it is dark glass inside a rim of the page's colour, so lemon, pink and amber never dilute to khaki or wine. #6dff9c lights only the mark, 'mind', Send, focus, the monitors, her screens, live lamps, the lit 'now' and the occupied track.
decisions: Tokens are the parent's except screen, which goes back to exactly #6dff9c, with glow and screenGlow at 1.0. That restores the tube's triple-halo VT323, the radar's sweep afterglow, blips, hub and bloom, her glyph screen's glow and scanlines, the greeting's pool, the key word's halo and Send's pool at the original strength.

A system rule for light on the diagram, written at the head of the relit block. The lamp where you are now is lit, and the section of track it stands on is lit from that lamp, fading into the steel toward the next stop (--track-lit). A chain that is live end to end is lit between its lit lamps. Everything else is steel. The rule is applied to Coming up (across on the desktop, down on the phone), To do on Home and on its own page, the plans list's today, the setup steps' next step, Chat's last stretch into the your-turn ring (the phone too), and Status's Who answers.

To do now tells the time. Late stops are filled amber with amber stamps, as the legend and Home say. A breathing now lamp sits on the rail between the last late stop and the first to come, in a wider gap, with the section to the next stop lit. Its margin stamp is the one lit word of the timetable, a lowercase 'now' in phosphor with a two-layer halo, so the margin reads '27 Sep 19:56, 28 Sep 19:56, now, 1 Oct 19:56'. The same drawing is on Home's To do. With nothing late, the now lamp heads the line, as it heads Coming up.

Status, Who answers: the rail between two lit lamps glows in the phosphor, and the stretch from the last one that answers fades into the steel toward the red 'If that one cannot'. The chain can be read at a glance from across the room.

The lamps are lit (E20). Every lamp the legend lights #6dff9c is a white-hot core (the brand 42% into white) inside a 5px bloom, a 14px halo and a 30px haze. A lamp breathes in its halo, never in its core, down to a low that is still light (4px, 12px at 50%, 24px at 16%), so it reads as on at any phase.

E12: the case spills its tube's light (0 0 90px -30px at 52% of the phosphor). This is the change that shows at half size beside Home's Next up, round Ideas' radar, the spend monitor, sign-in and the 404. The power light is a lamp with a hot core, and it follows --phosphor, so the spend monitor's amber and red follow it too.

Her screen at full strength wherever she appears (E19): the Vera title screen, the chat avatars (outside the rail's knock-out ring), Home's speaker, and now her card icon on Settings. In each of her bubbles her light pools in from the corner she speaks from: a 9% screen radial over the green-black glass, with a 10% top edge and no pattern under the words.

Home's box goes back to the original's single resting halo (E4, 38px at -20px, 60%). At rest, Send and the monitor are the greeting's two lit things. Every box lights in lit sage while someone types in it.

Terminus rings are small lit screens (E11): a raster 1px in 3, a centre of accent glass and a glowing glyph. On a section with its own colour, the rim and the glass are one screen and the light stays tight (18px at -7px). Warm sections get dark glass (6% to 3%) in an 88% rim, with the halo at 35%.

On the radar is typeset like a figure. The tube keeps only what it shows, with its lines at the 1.2rem floor. How to read it ('North at the top. Rings at 15 min, 45 min and 2 h by road.') is the figure's caption under the case, in DM Mono 0.75rem in the label steel, at 34ch with text-wrap: pretty. The cursor moves to the end of the last line in the tube, and no words change.
Plans month: a day has one 'now'. When today has a plan, the plan's lamp is it and the lamp by the day numeral is hidden. It stays only on an empty today.

Kept whole from the parent: the ring-and-bracket page heads, the Coming up main line, To do's timetable margin with one 'DUE' legend, Chat hung from Vera's mark and ending in a ring, steel reverse video for 'here', square matte slate plates, cream Archivo 84% heads, DM Sans for what people say, DM Mono tabular for stamps, VT323 on the tubes only, and 2.75rem targets (1 of 56 on Home under 44px).

Access, as the kit gives it. Reduced motion stops every breath through the base sheet's rule, and the lamps then sit at full glow. More contrast drops the title tile's raster and glow, her screens' halos, the bubble pool, Home's resting halo, the blip and hub glow, the tube's blur and the lit 'now''s halo, and keeps the lamps. designs.name: Pocket Timeline
designs.tagline: A family handheld: four greens, pixel sprites and chunky boxes, every page strung along one timeline with NOW lit on it.
designs.concept: The page is a family Game Boy. The slate plastic hardware (bar, foot, bezels, buttons) carries berry and indigo lens trims, and it frames a screen drawn in four greens. Everything hangs from one spine down the left. The title tile is the first stop and each section is a square stop. Anything with a time sits on the spine at that time: date tiles, ticks, speakers, settings pages as metro stops. NOW is a steady berry power light, NEXT is a green lamp that breathes, LATER is a hollow dashed stop, and past LATER the line runs on dotted. It should feel toy-like and friendly, and calmer now. The phosphor light (bloom, blur, scanlines, dot matrix, afterglow) is kept for the lit screens, the mark and the few lit controls.
designs.companions: Berry (#e57694, OKLCH 0.70/0.14/4; deep #752941) is the handheld's power light and now only says "you are here". It marks NOW on Home and above Chat's box, today's tile and box on Plans, overdue tasks, the power LED on every bezel, and the upper trim line under the bar and above the foot. As the shows/wishes colour it also marks the kids' names, the gift icon and the Wishes section. Slate (#151923 bar, #232631 bezel, #2d3140 hover) is the plastic: bar, foot, monitor cases, the sign-in and 404 handheld body, secondary buttons, starters, tabs and the family's chat bubbles. Indigo (#464f8c) is only the second trim line. Pea (#b2c38a) is the grounded structural green of labels, stop squares, tags, dates and heading icons. Moss (#404d33 edge, #556345 stop, #364228 spine) draws the chunky edges and the spine. Sage (#b3d6ab) is the link accent on Home, Status and Settings. The section and kind colours are low-chroma shell-plastic tones: grape, teal, dandelion, amber and rust. Outing is a pale mint (#85e9b6) so it stays apart from yellow and amber under deuteranopia.
decisions: Clean sheet (variants/r11-wild-1/sheet.css, about 106 KB) plus five templates: home.html, plans_month.html, tasks.html (new this round), login.html and 404.html. Every other page is styled from today's markup. I checked the system rules on pages I did not template (Plans list, Wishes, Family, Setup, AI model, Personality, the full Status page, and To do on a phone) with my own variant server.

The spine is a system rule. main carries a 4px moss line at var(--spine), solid, then dotted for the last 4rem. Stops are placed from any depth with position:absolute and only `left` set. Things with a time sit on the spine: date tiles, month day tiles, To do ticks (now carrying their time), Setup step numbers, chat avatars and her screen (each now joined to its bubble by a rail), and the Settings side-nav as metro stops. On Home the line column stretches to the shelf's height. A LATER stop (hollow dashed square, 'All plans →') ends what is planned, and from there the line is drawn dotted to the bottom.

Two materials of type. What the SCREEN shows is in pixel faces, set only at sizes where their pixels land whole. Pixelify Sans (a pixel is about 100/1000 em) runs at 40 for h1, 30 for h2, the month head, Home's question and the tile's day number, and 20 for panel heads, h3, item titles, cartridges, events, section cards, choices, names on Family, setup steps and avatars. Silkscreen (125/1000 em) is set only at 16px, for NOW/NEXT/LATER (with 2px tracking, one whole font pixel), dates, week labels, day names, TODAY, IN 2 DAYS, tags and timestamps. What is PRINTED ON THE PLASTIC is Nunito 800, the toy's rounded print: bar nav, buttons, tabs, starters, section links. Everything read at length is Nunito: 16/1.55 body, 18 lede, 15/700 labels, legends and table heads in pea, and 13 for the long small print (legal, crumbs, ids, 'used …', optional, changed) with tabular figures. VT323 stays on the lit screens. The 8px Silkscreen bezel legend sits on its 1px grid.

Frames have a budget. Tier A, what you hold, keeps the chunky frame and hard 4px shadow: the ask box (double frame), shelf panels, cartridges, section cards, choices and today on Plans. Tier B, rows on the line (Home's and the Plans list's coming-up rows, the month's non-today days, To do rows), have no box. The tile or tick is the row's frame, a 2px dashed line-2 rule parts rows, and surface-2 shows only on hover. A panel that only holds such rows (.panel:has(> .agenda)) loses its box. Tier C: tags are bare Silkscreen in their colour, and only a warning tag keeps a frame. Vera's bubble keeps one 3px moss edge and no inner line.

Phosphor kit kept whole where the screen is lit: each .crt is a handheld lens (slate bezel, big bottom-right radius, berry/indigo trim, PHOSPHOR DISPLAY legend, berry power LED) round a tube with 80px spill, three-layer text-shadow, 0.35px blur, scanlines plus dot-matrix columns, sheen and vignette, dim/bright/inverse, blinking block cursor, radar sweep, blips and ping, the 404 flicker and the sign-in face's blink. Also kept: the mark's glow and cursor, the lit A button with ring, pool and afterglow, the glowing 'mind', Home's box lit from the bottom-left through scanlines, cartridge afterglow in the kind's colour, her screen glyphs and the breathing lamps. The reduced-motion, more-contrast and forced-colours blocks are kept.

Chat reads down the spine. Every speaker hangs from it on the same side, with a 4px rail from avatar to bubble. The family's slate bubbles step in 2.5rem (1.25rem on a phone), like a reply, so slate against moss tells family from Vera. The name comes first, timestamps are Silkscreen 16 in pea (lavender-grey on slate, 6.3:1), and the measure is 62ch.

To do carries time on the spine. Each row opens with a Silkscreen eyebrow built in the template from due_input: 'SUN 27 SEP · 19:56', with the weekday worked out by Sakamoto's method in Jinja arithmetic. An undated task says SOMEDAY. The ISO 'Due …' span is gone, and the tick on the spine sits level with the eyebrow. The count is a Nunito sentence, not a stop, and the rows run the full width.

Plans month: runs of quiet weeks fold into one line ('31 Aug – 27 Sep · Nothing on.' instead of four). Tiles read month / day / weekday on both Plans and Home. Today keeps its berry-framed box and the other days are unboxed rows.

Controls: base-select picker with the lit pixel cursor. Pixel checkbox and radio. Buttons with a 3D bevel and a hard base that sink when pressed. Notched fields that light when typed in. The tick button is now a whole 44px target with its 30px pixel box drawn inside it. Tabs, starters, the From select, section links, bar tools, menu rows, the brand and the settings nav are all at least 44px tall, and row title links get vertical padding for a finger-sized hit area.

firstDraft.name: Pocket Timeline
firstDraft.concept: The page is a pocket console. The hardware (the bar, the foot, the bezel round every green screen, the buttons that aren't the main one) is slate plastic trimmed with the old handheld's two lens lines, berry and indigo. Between them is the screen, drawn in four greens that each have a job, and everything hangs from one spine down the left. The title tile is the first stop, each section is a square stop, and anything with a time sits on the spine at that time: date tiles, ticks, speakers, settings pages as metro stops. NOW is a berry power light and NEXT is a green lamp that breathes. It should feel toy-like and friendly, like a family's Game Boy. The phosphor light comes back only where the screen is lit: the LCDs bloom, blur, scanline and ghost, the mark glows and its cursor blinks.

designs.name: Night Gallery
designs.tagline: The family's page hung like an exhibition after hours: one size of type, a wall label for everything, and the green screens as the lit exhibits.
designs.concept: A museum after closing. The walls are dark and every word hangs as a label. Each room's name runs down a dyed, swallowtail-cut banner in the margin, under its small lit lamp. The green screens are the exhibits, each on a plinth under a warm picture light. The rule that makes it is ONE type size for every word: 22px on a desktop, 20px on a tablet and 18px on a phone, with one leading per step (1.4 wide, 1.5 below). Every space is that line, halved or doubled. Hierarchy comes only from weight, colour, case and space, so the page is calm and large-print, and the bright green reads as light that means something.
designs.companions: Brass (label #bdbf8e, accent #b8bc90, OKLCH hue 110) is the classifying voice. It sets section heads, dates, catalogue numbers, who spoke and when, every field label (filters, forms, settings and sign-in alike), the menu's top edge and Home's banner. The same hue, dark, is the material: olive plinths (#171812) and putty monitor cases (#39392e). A warm lamp white (#c5bf9a) is used only in the picture lights. The four house rooms are now told apart by material: Home is brass cloth. Vera's room is a strip of her screen: glass, scanlines and VT323 lit green, the one lit banner. Status is the monitors' putty plastic (bezel mixed toward #dcc4a4, moulded, no weave). Settings is iron (edge mixed toward #98abbd, brushed, with two rivets). Each family room keeps a grounded pigment: heather #b395d7 (Ideas, events), slate #87cfe8 (Plans, trips, date numerals), ochre #f4cc64 (To do, activities), rose #e99dbe (Wishes, shows, kids), copper #eea05d (Family, restaurants, today, needs a look), terracotta #e88671 (seasonal), sage #7ed3a6 (outing). They appear at 45% into the black on the banners and now also on the 2px rails under each section, and in full only in small-cap kind labels, date numerals, the today tile and the lamps. The 404 and 403 banners are dyed from danger #ea6a64. Bone ink #e1e0d6 carries the words. The bright #6dff9c is kept for light: the mark and cursor, 'mind', one lit key per view, focus, the lamps, the tubes, her screen and banner, and the ask box's lit corner. The calmer #92dfa7 (lit) is for ticked, typed and done.
decisions: ONE SIZE, taken literally: font-size inherits from html everywhere, form controls, code and the tab bar included. The smallest measured text is 18px on a phone and 22px on a desktop.

One leading per step, and the whole space scale follows it: --l = calc(var(--lh) * 1rem), with --h, --q, --l2, --l3 and --l4 derived from --l. --lh is 1.4 at 70rem and 1.5 below, so the 22px step no longer spends 33px lines in dead gaps.
Two bends of the roll, as before. Case includes synthesised small caps. The only lettering drawn larger is aria-hidden picture on the glass (the 404, the spend figure, the radar labels).

Small capitals now hold their colour. Chrome builds Archivo's small caps by scaling the capitals, so every small-cap role (eyebrows, kinds, dates, who-and-when, ids, th, caption, h3, tags and field labels) uses --sc-weight 740 and --sc-stretch 108% on Archivo's width axis. Keys are set at 780 and 108%.

One classifying voice. Every field label (.field > label, .setting-head label, legend, the sign-in form's labels) is now brass small caps, like the filters' SEARCH, KIND and SHOW. label.check keeps its sentence in ink, because it reads as what it says. Italics are gone for good: em is weight 560 in ink, since hierarchy here is weight.

A banner for every room. A new room_banner(name, glyph, cls) macro in _ui.html draws an aria-hidden banner-head (lamp plus banner, hidden on a phone). Home uses it, and so do sign-in ('Entrance', brass), 404 and 403 ('Room 404' and 'Room 403', a museum's room numbers, dyed from danger), the idea page ('Ideas', heather) and the three setup pages ('Installation', the museum's word for hanging a show and the software's for setting up). The h1s on sign-in, 404 and setup now take the room-name tier (800, caps, tracked).

An idea's own page is its object label hung large. A 3px rule dyed 45% from the idea's kind runs across the top. Its #number, kind and status sit above its sentence-case name, then the tombstone facts under a middle dot, then two lines of wall. The facts drop their icons, and the place below is its own labelled object ('THE PLACE' over a sentence-case name).

House rooms by material, not pigment. The banner is built from custom layers (--hem, --grain, --fold, --banner), so a room swaps its material: cloth, glass with scanlines, moulded putty, or brushed iron with rivets. Vera's halo sits on .room as a drop-shadow, because the clip-path eats the banner's own. Her name is VT323, held to Archivo's cap height with font-size-adjust: cap-height from-font, set on the parent so it computes in Archivo. The bar stays brass for all four.

Rails show the structure at a glance. .section-head, the tabs, the settings floor plan, To do's filters and every h2-headed panel on Status, Settings, the idea's side, Family, Memory and setup hang on a 2px rail dyed 45% from their room. On Home the rails are slate (Coming up), ochre (To do), heather (Lately added) and rose (wishes), so the entrance reads as a floor plan of the rooms that follow. The object labels' top rules moved to line-2 (#43443b), and line itself was lifted to #36362f.

The phosphor light is back on Home without a corner wash on the greeting. The guestbook stands beside the exhibit, so the tube lights it from its lower-left corner: a 12% brand radial, plus the kit's white 2.8% scanlines (1px in 4) on an isolated ::before at z-index -1 behind the words, masked to that corner and removed under more contrast. The exhibit's caption carries the E20 lamp, a breathing brand dot (8px, then 18px at 45%) that stays lit and still under reduced motion.

Status: the day's spend readout is now figure.exhibit with a plinth and picture light. .spend is off its olive panel, so all three screens (Next up, the radar, the readout) stand the same way on the wall, and the amber and red phosphor states are kept.

First screen: Home went from 2652px to 2346px (welcome, setup and wishes at --l2, dashboard row-gap --l2, main bottom --l3). The catalogue and the To do register use a row-gap of --l. Month cells are 3rem, so empty weeks shrink. To do's zone note stands over the register (flex or grid order) instead of at the door. Ledes are balanced at 40ch.

Controls: fields keep their glow focus. Checkboxes and radios get the page's own 2px brand outline with a lit edge, so focus on 'Send where I am' is visible (focus-14). The phone's tabs keep the one size through Archivo's width axis (font-stretch 85%, letter-spacing 0). The tools are 44px wide. The settings floor plan stays on a phone as a wrapped list without its pictograms. .status-open is dim, so the default state spends no pigment.

Setup is written for, not only shot: a page-setup class gives it a line of wall between each part, a rail under 'Left for later', and a tighter progress plan. The Family, Memory and Wishes rooms were checked by hand and pick up the rails and label voice.

strengths: A real type system on one size: 22/20/18px with one leading per step, and space derived from that line. Weight, case, brass and space carry the whole hierarchy, and small caps now match the lowercase in colour.

The banner system reaches every room, including the ones no tab names (sign-in, 404 and 403, an idea, setup). The house rooms are told apart by material: brass cloth, her glass, putty plastic and brushed iron. Vera's is the one lit banner.
Rails dyed from each room make the structure show at a glance. Home reads as a floor plan of the rooms that follow.

The phosphor light lives where the machine is: the full tube kit on every exhibit, the lit guestbook corner with scanlines, the breathing running lamp on the caption, 'mind', the one lit key, focus rings (now on checkboxes too) and Status's lamps. Everything else is grounded material.
Three green screens now stand the same way (Next up, the radar, the day's spend), each on a plinth under a warm picture light.

firstDraft.name: Night Gallery
firstDraft.concept: A museum after closing. The walls are dark and every word hangs as a label. Each room's name runs down a dyed, swallowtail-cut banner in the margin, under its small lit lamp. The green screens are the exhibits, each standing on a plinth under a warm picture light and spilling its own phosphor onto the plinth. The rule that makes it is ONE type size for every word, 22px on a desktop, 20px on a tablet and 18px on a phone, on one 1.5 leading. Hierarchy comes only from weight, colour, case and space, so the page feels calm, large-print and curated, and the bright green is light that means something.

designs.name: Flight Console
designs.tagline: The family's week run from a 1969 flight console: a violet flight-plan drawing leads every section, rows of lamps say how things stand, and the phosphor lights only what is live.
designs.concept: Every page is a console in a 1969 mission control room, built from three materials that each have one job. Grey console bays carry engraved condensed legends. Violet flight-plan drawings on a faint plotting grid lead every section: a full drawing where the picture shows something the words do not, and a 76px pictogram tile everywhere else. #6dff9c appears only as light: the tubes, a lit lamp, the lit key word, the primary key, focus. The page should feel calm and exact. You read how things stand from rows of lamps and small readouts before you read a word, and the green monitors glow the way the original page's did.
designs.companions: Ditto violet (OKLCH hue 305: #aa92c7 for lines and captions, #716085 for secondary lines, #3a3246 for the grid) has one job, the drawings: the flight-plan tracks, figure captions, the plotting-board dot grid, the pictogram tiles on settings cards and panels and on idea cards, and the chevrons on folds. It is never body text and never a fill. The Ideas section and the Event kind moved off it to periwinkle #8caaeb, so on the Ideas page violet is the drawing again. Amber (#eda653) means "now, or needs a look": the console clock, today on both tracks and the month, late or due-today tasks (words, lamp and card edge), the setup holds, the LATE and HOLDS readouts, and the Needs-a-look lamp. Red (#f26b61) now means failed and nothing else: a lit red lamp, a red ring only under Needs attention or Worth a look, and errors. The kind and section colours (yellow, cyan, pink, coral, periwinkle, soft green) are lamp lenses: small coloured squares beside a kind's engraved name and on each console's name plate. Cyan also lights the lamp under each day that has a plan on the month's track. The neutrals are a slightly green console grey with warm off-white ink.
decisions: Clean sheet (variants/r11-wild-3/sheet.css, about 103 KB), with 15 templates of my own: base, _ui, _settings, settings/general, home, chat, ideas, idea, idea_form, plans_month, tasks, status, settings, settings_section, login. removed.txt is empty: no form, field, link or icon was removed, and every kept form keeps its csrf and once tokens.

Pictures come in two sizes, chosen by what the picture can show. A full drawing (a strip across a bay, or the 250px column) is used only where it informs: Home's four-week track, the month's track, the two radars and the other tubes, the crew board, the annunciator, the spend tube, and the new-idea card. Every other section is led by the Settings cards' 76px plotting-board tile with its pictogram, in slim bays (.bay.slim) and tiled panels (.panel.tiled): Home's setup, wishes and Lately added; the chat's loop; every settings panel (a pictogram per group, in _settings.html); the lower Status panels; and the idea detail page, which is led by its kind's own pictogram. On a phone the tiles step aside.

One lamp language on every page, written into _ui.html as lamp(), task_lamp() and task_legend(): lit phosphor is live, working or done; amber is now or needs a look; unlit is waiting or open; a dark hollow ring is off or called off; lit red, and only red, is failed. Every lamp has words beside it.

Plans, the 'Flight plan' console, now leads with the flight plan itself: Home's track laid over the days the calendar shows. It has a tick a day, hatched weekends, month names, a lit NOW line, and a numbered stop for each plan joined to the next by an arc, with the next stop lit and past ones faded. Under each day number is a lamp: cyan for a day with a plan, amber for today. The stop numbers are printed on the calendar's events, so the drawing and the grid key together. On October it shows six stops across the month.

The To do crew board uses the same lamp code and legend as Home's, so under the default Open filter it shows the two late tasks in amber. The page works lateness out itself: the demo has no 'late' field on the tasks page, so the template counts days from the sign-in clock, using each deadline's own UTC offset. Late cards say 'Was due 2 days ago' in amber, with an amber lamp in the corner, an amber edge, and the exact time in mono underneath. The OPEN pill shows only when a task's status differs from the filter.

Status follows the dark-cockpit convention. A normal annunciator window stays dark, with a small lit lamp and its legend in ink. An off window is dark, with a ring for a lamp and a #7f8a84 legend at 12px. Only a caution (amber) or an alarm (red) fills with light. Status lights hold steady, and only the one live thing breathes: the model answering the chat. 'No key' is a dark ring, not a red one. Green on Status fell from 47.5% to 13.9% of its colour.

Home's console: a readout rail with the console clock (TODAY, TUE 29 SEP in amber mono) where the 'FLIGHT 01' plate was. Legends are 12px, figures 20px, and the wordless rail lamps are gone, as is the date eyebrow by Vera. Her name sits level with the tube's top edge and the ways to start level with its bottom. The ask box takes up the height between them, which gives a taller page to write on instead of a gap. Tab still reaches the textarea straight after the bar.

Plex Sans is for reading (16/1.55). Plex Mono is kept to figures and times (tabular, slashed zero). VT323 appears only on the tubes. Home's agenda dropped its day block, since the stop number and the track give the day, and now sets each date as two steady lines in the condensed face ('Thursday 1 October, 10:00', then 'in 2 days' dim), so the four columns line up.

The phosphor kit stays where the phosphor is: the mark's bloom and cursor, the top afterglow, Send's ring and pool, the lit key word, Home's box glowing at rest, the desk lit from below through scanlines, the full tube (glass, halos, blur, scanlines, sheen, vignette, power light, spill, power-on), the radar sweep, blips and pings, the 404 flicker, the sign-in face, her falling glyphs, lamps with a two-layer halo, and the 1.2s afterglow. Page heads: the plate and the breadcrumb share one row, the crumbs in the plate's right-hand slot, so a page inside another stacks two levels over its title, not three. The same row leads the idea detail page. The settings nav's caption is a real figcaption with the shared 'FIG. N' numbering.

firstDraft.name: Flight Console
firstDraft.concept: Every page is a console in a 1969 mission control room, built from three materials that each have one job. Grey console bays carry engraved condensed legends. Violet flight-plan drawings, printed as in ditto ink on a faint plotting grid, lead every section. The #6dff9c phosphor shows up only as light: the tubes, a lit lamp, the lit key word, the primary key, focus. The page should feel calm and exact. You read how things stand from rows of lamps and small readouts before you read a word, and the green monitors glow the way the original page's did.

designs.name: Videotex Sommaire
designs.tagline: The family's own videotex service: one thing at a time under a mosaic band, numbered contents, a row of keys along the foot of every screen, and the phosphor lit on its terminal.
designs.concept: FamilyDB is set out as a 1980s videotex service like the Minitel. Every screen opens with a band holding the page's mosaic picture, its name in double-height VT323 and its page-number tile, then shows one large thing, with a row of brown-plastic keys along the foot. Home is the terminal itself: a green tube fills the first screen above the keys, with Next up and a large radar at the top and the question and a blinking cursor at the foot of the glass, and a numbered Contents list sits beside it. The feel is a warm, calm public-service terminal where only the machine gives off green light.
designs.companions: Straw (hue 92: #e9d487 accent, #f2eacc heading, #beb491 label, #d0cbb5 secondary) is the service's own voice. It takes headings, labels, key legends, the number tiles, and the Home, Vera, Status and Settings bands. Brown plastic (#382b1f bezel, #15130e deck, and a warm key gradient) is the machine's body: every monitor case, Home's terminal, the key row, the keys, selects, tabs and starters, and the docked Save bar and chat input line. Low-chroma material colours mark the sections, each running through its band, dither ramp, key tile, contents line and kind: ochre #eaa76b (people, restaurants, today, needs a look), sea teal #83d5d4 (To do), cornflower #9ccdf8 (plans), heather #bc97e8 (ideas), dusty rose #eda6c1 (wishes), brick #e68677 (seasonal) and moss #9bcf89 (outings). #6dff9c appears only on the phosphor and on live things: the tubes, the mark and its caret, Send and the other primary keys, focus, lamps, the LED on the current key, the box being typed in, and her screen. A calmer #92dfa7 is used for ticks, OK and done.
decisions: A clean sheet (104 KB) with my own base, _ui, home, _ask, ideas and tasks templates, a redrawn 12x12 mosaic sprite (all 51 ids kept, plus m-* separated-block versions) and a ramp.svg mask. removed.txt is empty, and every form keeps its csrf and once tokens.

One spine on every screen: the key row (Home, Vera, Ideas, Plans, To do, Wishes) is sticky at the foot of every page, Home's included, and now 60px tall on desktop. Anything a page must keep in reach docks flush onto it, as line 24 of a Minitel was the input line: General's Save bar is in the deck's plastic with no bottom border, and the chat's one-line tube with its keys is sticky at bottom: var(--keys-h).

Home's first screen is only the terminal. .welcome has min-height calc(100svh - bar - keys - 3.5rem), and the minitel stretches as a flex column so the question and prompt sit at the foot of the glass and Next up sits at the top beside a radar of up to 18.5rem. The first part starts under the fold (.welcome + .frame margin), so in the full-page shot the sticky key row lands exactly under the terminal as its keyboard rather than across a frame.

One kind of head. The band (art tile, stretched title, page-number tile, dashed strip in the section colour) and Home's .frame-head (number tile, mosaic, head-size title, links, the same strip) share one anatomy. The dither ramp is masked with a second gradient layer (mask-composite: intersect) so it stops short of the right end, and the page number, ALL PLANS and ADD AN IDEA sit on clean band. The page number is said once: in row zero only where there is no band (Home P100, lost P404), in the band's tile everywhere else.

A VT323 scale of five steps with --tall: 1.4. Display is 4rem, stretched (band h1, 404, the spend figure). Head is 2.6rem, stretched (frame h2, Contents, one idea's name, sign-in, the date leaf's day). Sub is 2rem, flat (panel h2, folds, the question, the month, number tiles, avatars). Tube is 1.625rem and tube-s is 1.3rem, for the screens' words. Every earlier size (3.4, 3.2, 3, 2.5, 2.4, 2.1, 1.9, 1.5 and so on) now maps to one of these.

The family's face is now Red Hat Text, with a plain zero as the Minitel's character set drew it. It uses two title steps: --t-title 1.5rem for a line on a page (agenda, checklist, task, index) and --t-lead 1.3rem for a tile or menu line (idea tiles, restaurants, steps, settings parts, contents). The when-lines drop to body, so the title leads. Tabular figures are on .when, .meta, .event small, .chip, .said-by and table cells.

The machine's face (Martian Mono) is now semi-condensed everywhere, via the font shorthand keyword so no later font shorthand resets it, at 0.03em tracking (--track). It is closer to videotex's narrow letters, and it is the only face left that slashes its zero: tags, codes and keys.

The phosphor is where the machine is. The tube keeps the kit's three-layer halo, the 0.35px blur on the machine's words (not on typed text), scanlines, sheen, vignette, power light, sweep with afterglow, blips and ping, breathing lamps, her falling glyphs, the mark's bloom and caret, and the ring and bloom round the whole glass on focus. Added: the tube's block cursor after > while the line is empty and unfocused (kit E15), and her last line clamped to 3 lines. The phone keeps a 5.5rem radar beside NEXT UP and the title, using a display: contents grid.
Plans' month is a page turn: ← Earlier, September 2026 at the sub step, Later → (the month-nav set to display: contents and ordered), so the band stays the page's only display head.

Controls: square plastic keys with a 3px edge, and the mic now square too. Text inputs have a 3px bottom edge so they match the selects. The base-select picker has a straw ▶ checkmark. The fold inside a list line (Edit, complete, or snooze; Everything else; Move it) is a ghost key: sentence case, label colour, an outlined + tile. A fold that is a panel's whole content (Plan it, Put something on the calendar) opens on its heading, like a folded panel.

Numbered tiles as one idiom: Contents, Settings parts, the settings nav, tabs, setup steps, and now the wish lists (wish-top counters and .wish-rank tiles in rose) and the Family list, whose grid was broken (the Change key wrapped under the avatar) and is now tile, name and tags, how the bot knows them, Change.
designs.measures: 0 hard checks failed; 1 guideline missed: the page's words (Home differs by 8.8%, because of 'Contents' and the contents list naming each part a second time with its count; every other page differs by 0-1.4%). ink_on_bg 15.01, brand_on_bg 15.1, and the signature is unchanged (brand and screen both #6dff9c, 0.897/0.186/151.4; glow, screenGlow and topGlow all 1.0). Green share of colour / hue entropy: home 24.6% / 0.64, ideas 42.4% / 0.635, chat 17.2% / 0.542, status 5.5% / 0.573. Bright-green px per mille: home 2.49, ideas 10.09, chat 5.54, status 0.14. CIEDE2000 minimums: kinds 17.6 typical / 6.0 deuteranopia / 6.7 protanopia; sections 17.4 / 7.0 / 7.9. Smallest text is 12px (the phone key legends). No sideways scroll on any rendered page; I also checked 14 more pages at phone width by hand and fixed the one that overflowed (settings/general). Greeting pixels: (1150,120) = (11,15,13), plain bg beside the Contents column, since this design has no wash; (100,640) = (4,11,6), inside the terminal's tube glass.
strengths: Every screen now has the same spine: row zero, the band, one large thing, and the key row at the foot, which Home now has too. What a page must keep in reach (the chat's line, Settings' Save) docks flush on the keys as one console.

Home's first screen is one object, the brown Minitel, and its green tube is the brightest, most alive thing on the page: a large radar sweeping beside Next up, and the question with a blinking block cursor at the foot of the glass. The squint test finds the screen and Send first, then the numbered Contents.

The type is a real system with named steps: five VT323 steps with one --tall stretch, two title steps and a body in Red Hat Text, and semi-condensed Martian Mono labels. Every page, Plans, To do and Settings included, draws from the same tokens.

Colour has clear jobs: straw is the service, brown plastic is the machine, low-chroma material colours mark the sections, and bright green is only the phosphor and live things. Status is 5.5% green, Home 24.6%, and the tube is where the light is.
Numbered tiles and the dashed foot strip are one idiom across Contents, Home's parts, Settings, tabs, setup steps, wish lists and the Family list, and the numbering is said once per page.
The chat's first view is band, thread and a docked one-line input on the keys, the most compact chat view in the design so far.
weaknesses: Home is still long (3574px against today's 2111). That is partly the idea (the terminal takes the whole first screen, and each part is spaced as its own page), but the Coming up and To do rows remain generous.

When the demo has no last line from her, Home's stretched tube leaves about 100px of empty glass between the radar and the question on a 900px screen. It reads as a screen, but it is space the design pays for.

The sticky key row is drawn where the first viewport ends in the full-page shots of long pages. I placed Home so it lands under the terminal, but on the Family, Plans list and Personality full-page captures it crosses the content (real scrolling is fine).
On the phone, the chat's docked console (tube, select with mic and Send, then Send where I am) takes about 30% of the screen above the keys.
VT323 has no distinct curly apostrophe, so 'The kids’ wishes' still looks almost straight in the tube face.
One idea's own page still uses its split panel head rather than the band, so it is the one page without the shared head anatomy.
Words: Home differs by 8.8% from today because of the Contents list, which is intrinsic to the sommaire idea.
revisions: 1 (foot row): I deleted `.page-home > .places { display: none }`, the `.places.under-terminal` rules and the keyrow('home', 'under-terminal') call, so Home has the same sticky row as every page. I slimmed it on desktop: --keys-h 4.5rem to 3.75rem, keys at min-height 2.75rem, icon tiles smaller. Row zero plus keys is now 108px.

2 (docking): `.save-bar` now sits at bottom: var(--keys-h) with border-bottom 0 and the --deck background, as one console with the keys. `.page-chat .ask` is sticky at bottom: var(--keys-h) with a one-line tube (padding 0.6rem 1rem, textarea min-height 1.3em) and a compact deck. The Vera band is at min-height 5.5rem with the h1 at the head step, and the chat page-head margin is 1.5rem. On the phone, the chat deck puts the select, mic and Send on one row.

3 (numbering and heads): .page-code shows only on Home (P100) and the lost page (P404). The .folio is gone from the frame heads, and the pages count with it. .frame::before is replaced by the band's coloured foot strip under .frame-head (ramp moved to ::before, strip to ::after on both). .frame margin-top is 4rem. The ramp gets a second mask layer, linear-gradient(to left, transparent 0 var(--clear), #000 +5rem), with mask-composite: intersect (clear 9rem on bands, 17rem on frame heads).

4 (VT323 scale): added --tall: 1.4 and --t-sub: 2rem (plus --t-tube-s), and mapped every tube size onto display, head, sub, tube or tube-s. The month-head h2 is at sub, flanked by Earlier and Later as a page turn. 'The kids’ wishes' is written with ’ in the contents line and in the frame_head call.

5 (read steps and labels): list titles now use two steps (--t-title 1.5rem for page lines, --t-lead 1.3rem for tiles and menu lines). All Martian Mono is semi-condensed at 0.03em, using the font shorthand keyword so later shorthands do not reset it. The rail summary on Ideas has text-wrap: balance and its second icon hidden.
6 (zeros): --read is now Red Hat Text (plain zero, good bold), with tabular-nums on .when, .meta, .event small, .chip, .said-by and table cells. The slashed zero is left only in the machine's face.

7 (phosphor): the block cursor now blinks after > while the line is empty and unfocused. Her last line is clamped to 3 lines. The phone keeps a 5.5rem radar beside NEXT UP and the title. On Ideas, .on-radar moved to the top of the rail. I also went further than the note: the terminal now fills Home's first screen, with the question at the foot of the glass and the radar enlarged.

8 (tidying): the wishes count sums kid.open. 'Sommaire' became 'Contents' in head-size double height. The setup line's ▲ is replaced by the warning mosaic icon. button.mic is square. Text inputs have a 3px bottom in --edge. details.more > summary is a ghost key (label colour, sentence case, an outlined + tile, no fill), and a panel-level fold opens on its heading. The Family list's grid is fixed, with the initial as a tile, and the wish lists are numbered in rose.

Beyond the notes: settings/general overflowed sideways on the phone (1fr grid columns, long code). I fixed it with minmax(0, 1fr) and overflow-wrap on code. I also added spacing between stacked .setting blocks, heads for each kid on the Wishes page, a gap in the fact labels, a Plans header that stacks on the phone, and the new blur target and ramp hidden in more-contrast mode.
Declined in part: none of the notes betrayed the idea, so I acted on all of them. The design name 'Videotex Sommaire' stays in the palette file, but the page says 'Contents', as the critic asked.
crit: 1. Give Home the same foot row as every other page. On desktop Home, `.page-home > .places { display: none }` hides the fixed row of keys, and `keyrow("home", "under-terminal")` scrolls away with the terminal. From Coming up onwards the only way to Ideas or Plans is back at the top. Delete that rule and the `.places.under-terminal` call in home.html: the terminal's `.deck` is already its keyboard. The row is the design's spine and has to be the same object on every screen. While there, slim it on desktop (`--keys-h: 4.5rem` down to about `3.75rem`, `.places .key` min-height 2.75rem). Row zero plus the deck currently take 120px of a 900px screen.

2. Dock onto the key row flush, the way line 24 of a Minitel was the input line. First, General: `.save-bar { bottom: calc(var(--keys-h) + 0.75rem) }` leaves a 12px slot, and 'Exact position and travel times' slices through it between the two bars. Use `bottom: var(--keys-h)` with `border-bottom: 0` and the `--deck` background, so the Save bar sits on the keys as one console. Second, Chat: at 1280×900 the input terminal starts at y=767, under the keys. Make `.page-chat .ask` sticky at `bottom: var(--keys-h)` with a one-line tube (`.ask-screen .crt-tube { padding: .6rem 1rem }`, textarea `min-height: 1.3em`). Also shrink the Vera band (`.page-chat .band { min-height: 5.5rem }`, h1 at the head step) and cut `.page-chat .page-head { margin-bottom: 3rem }` to 1.5rem, so the first view is band, thread and input line.

3. Keep one numbering system and one kind of head, and trim the chrome. Drop `.page-code` from row zero on pages that have a band: P200 beside a '200' tile says the same thing twice. Keep it only on Home, which has no band. Drop the `.folio` 1/5 to 5/5 from Home's frames, because the `.frame-no` tile already matches the sommaire number. Replace `.frame::before` (a grey dashed rule 3rem above, which doubles the band's own border) with the same coloured foot strip as `.band::after` under `.frame-head`, and cut `.frame { margin-top: 6.5rem }` to about 4rem. Home is 3793px tall against today's 2111. Finally, stop the dither ramp (`.band::before`, `.frame-head::after`) short of the right edge by adding a second mask layer, `linear-gradient(to left, transparent 0 9rem, #000 14rem)` with `mask-composite: intersect`. Then '300', '990', 'ALL PLANS →' and 'ADD AN IDEA' sit on clean band instead of on texture.

4. Build a VT323 scale with steps. Today there are about twelve tube sizes (4, 3.4, 3.2, 3, 2.6, 2.5, 2.4, 2.1, 2, 1.9, 1.5rem) and four different double-height stretches (`.page-title h1` 1.45, `.lost h1` 1.4, `.sommaire-title`/`.month-head h2` 1.35, `.frame-head h2`/`.idea-main h1` 1.3). Define `--tall: 1.4` and three steps. Display is `--t-h1` for the band h1 and the 404. Head is `--t-head` for frame h2, the sommaire title and idea h1. Sub is 2rem, unstretched, for panel h2, `details.panel > summary` and `.ask-question`. On Plans, `.month-head h2` (3.2rem ×1.35) stacks a second display heading under the band's 'Plans'. Set it at the sub step and flank it with the Earlier/Later keys (← September 2026 →) as a page turn. Fix the straight apostrophe VT323 draws in "The kids' wishes" (home.html, the sommaire line and the frame_head call) by writing it with ’, which the question already uses.

5. Typeset the family's words in fewer steps and tighten the machine's labels. List titles in Atkinson take six sizes: `.agenda .what` 1.75, `.checklist .what`/`.task-head h2`/`.card-main h2` 1.6, `.idea-cards strong`/`.restaurants-link strong` 1.45, `.steps-list a` 1.35, `.section-what strong` 1.3, `ol.sommaire .what` 1.2rem. Use two: `--t-title` (1.5rem) for a line on a page and `--t-lead` (1.3rem) for a tile or menu line. The Martian Mono labels (`.eyebrow`, `label`, `.places .key`, `.kind`, `.tag`, `.said-by`) are wide and tracked 0.05–0.08em, which makes 'SOMETHING TO EAT' and 'TUESDAY 29 SEPTEMBER' sprawl. Use the face's width axis instead, `font-variation-settings: "wdth" 87.5` at 0.03em tracking, which is closer to videotex's narrow letters and gives the phone room back. On Ideas, `.rail details.panel > summary` wraps 'Save a thought for / later': add `text-wrap: balance` and hide its second icon (the sparkle beside the + tile).

6. Deal with the slashed zeros. Atkinson Hyperlegible slashes every zero in the family's own lines ('10:00', '$0.00', '0 open', 'Due 2026-09-27'), and Martian Mono does too ('IN 10 DAYS', 'P000'). Videotex's own character set drew a plain 0, so this reads as a DEC or IBM terminal habit rather than a Minitel one. Switch `--read` to a sturdy humanist sans with a plain zero and a good bold, such as Red Hat Text or Hanken Grotesk, with `tabular-nums` on `.when`, `.meta`, `.event small` and `.chip`. Leave the slashed zero only where the machine speaks: tags and codes.

7. Finish the phosphor on the terminal. First, add the tube's block cursor (kit E15, which today's Next up had) after the prompt while the box is empty and unfocused, so the glass says 'type here': `.prompt-line:has(textarea:placeholder-shown):not(:focus-within) .prompt-mark::after { content:""; display:inline-block; width:.45em; height:.62em; margin-left:.2em; background:var(--phosphor); box-shadow:0 0 8px var(--phosphor); animation: blink 1.06s steps(1) 10 }`. Second, her last line was never rendered, so clamp `.crt .thread.brief .said-text` to 3 lines (`-webkit-line-clamp`); a long reply must not push the question off the first screen. Third, on the phone keep a small radar (5.5rem, floated right of the title) instead of `.next-up .radar { display: none }`, since it is the tube's best picture. Fourth, on Ideas move `.on-radar` to the top of `.rail`: its first view currently has no green screen at all.

8. Tidy Home's sommaire and the small keys. The wishes line shows '2' (the number of kids) beside "The kids' wishes" while both kids show '0 open'. In home.html, count the open wishes (the sum of `kid.open`) instead. 'Sommaire' is the one French word on an English page and means nothing to a family who called the original 'the Matrix'. Use 'Contents' in the same VT323 double-height. Replace `.to-setup .what::after { content: " ▲" }`, which reads as 'up' or 'sort', with the warning mosaic the frame already uses. `button.mic` is the only round key in a square system, so give it the key's corners. The select's 3px bottom edge makes it 2px taller than the input beside it (General, New idea): give text inputs a 3px bottom in `--edge`. On To do, the per-task `details.more > summary` 'EDIT, COMPLETE, OR SNOOZE' is a long uppercase filled key that outweighs the title. Make it a ghost key (no fill, `--label`, sentence case), and carry the numbered-tile idiom to the Family list (`.people .avatar`) and the wish lists (`.wish-list` rows numbered like `.steps-list li::before` in `--shows`).

firstDraft.name: Videotex Sommaire
firstDraft.concept: FamilyDB is set out as a 1980s videotex service like the Minitel. Every screen has a row zero with the page number (P100 to P990), a band with the page's mosaic picture and its title in double-height pixel letters, one big thing, and a row of keys under it. Home is the terminal itself: a brown-plastic Minitel whose green screen shows Next up with its radar and her question, and you type straight onto the phosphor. Beside it sits a numbered sommaire, and Home's other parts follow as paginated pages 1/5 to 5/5. It should feel like a warm, slightly nostalgic public-service terminal, calm and flat, where the green light comes only from the machine.

designs.name: Tuning Dock
designs.tagline: Docked Terminal set on a perfect fourth, six sizes and nothing between them, with every page's dock a console: the keys that tune the desk at its head, the machine's answer lit on the glass at its foot.
designs.concept: A calm terminal on a desk at night. Every page has a lit glass dock of the same width, and every dock is a console with one rule: at its head sit the keys that choose what the desk shows (a view, a month, the filters), and at its foot the machine's answer glows on a tube. That answer is Next up, the radar, the tally, the spend or the page being set. Pressing a key latches it, the tubes glow at full phosphor, and the slate desk mat stays quiet. Only the lit things are green, and the largest type on any page belongs to the machine.
designs.companions: Indigo is the family's hand. It marks a key that acts (starters, Filter, Earlier and Later, the mic), a latched key, and the bar's current place. Slate (#252e35 to #151b20) is for choice banks (Kind, For, Show, View, the settings column, the tabs) and, new in this revision, for keys that only go somewhere (Home's All plans, All 4, All, Add an idea, All 12). In a bank only the key that is down takes colour. A kind key that is down is lit in its own kind's colour: amber restaurant, lemon activity, sage #86d9a6 outing, cyan trip and day trip, pink show, coral seasonal, lilac event and other. That matches the rows' inlays and wide-caps kind words, so the bank works as the legend. A cobalt wash (#4f60e6) sits in the dock's top corner, opposite the green pool and scanlines at its foot. The ink is bone (#d4cfc4) with headings in #ebe6da. Labels are blue-grey (#a4b0c2), tinted 22% toward the phosphor inside the console. The setup panel's edge is amber, and overdue dates on To do are amber. Bright #6dff9c stays on the mark and caret, Send, Add an idea and the other primary keys, the key word 'mind', the focus ring, the live lamps (READY, WHO ANSWERS, the settings STATUS lamp) and every tube.
decisions: Type scale: a perfect fourth (1.333) with six steps: 12 note, 16 text, 21.3 head, 28.4 title, 37.9 page, 50.5 show. build.py moves every size in today's stylesheet onto the scale in place, then appends the design's own rules. variants/r11-wmut-1/sizes.sh probed 19 pages at 1280px and 4 at 390px after this revision, and every visible size landed on a step. Every h1 is now the page step (37.9/42). The show step (50.5) is used only for a tube's one figure: the spend, the To do tally, the Restaurants tally and the 404. So the largest thing on any page is lit.

Hierarchy that the scale does not carry goes to Archivo's width axis: 74-78% for display, 100% for reading, 106-118% for small caps. Red Hat Mono with tabular slashed-zero figures sets the facts. VT323 is kept for the glass. Leading sits on a 6px grid.

One console rule, written in the sheet and applied on every page. The head holds every key that changes what the desk shows and nothing else. The foot holds the machine's answer on glass. The desk holds the things themselves and the keys that act on them. Ideas: fields and banks at the head, the radar at the foot. To do: Search and Filter plus the Show bank, then a tally tube. Plans list: a View bank, then Next up. Plans month: a View bank, then the month by name with Earlier/Later, then Next up. Settings pages: a joined vertical bank of all nine pages, then a tube reading 'SETTINGS 1/9 / General / > Ready.' (Saved. or Not saved. after a post) and a breathing STATUS lamp. Settings overview: the spend tube from Status, parsed from the Spending card's own lines, and a PAGES lamp line with amber where a page needs a look. New idea form: the radar alone ('A new idea / > a blip once it has a place'). Restaurants: a tally tube. Status and Chat keep their own docks. The desk's left edge is now 488px on every page at 1280.

Where I bent the rule: the tabs between a section's two lists (All ideas / Restaurants) stay at the head of the list on the desk. I moved them into the Ideas console and measured it: the console went to about 980px and the radar fell below the fold again. They are 'two lists', not 'a drawing of one list', so they stay beside the count. Plans' List/Month is the drawing of one set of plans, so it moved into the console as the critic asked.

Ideas console: Search runs full width. Under it are Status, labelled at its side the way Home's FROM is, and the indigo Filter key that sends both. The Kind and For banks follow, then the radar. The whole console is 763px tall with a kind latched and Clear showing. It fits at 1280x900, so it is sticky again under min-height 56rem. What made it fit: the dock is widened to 27rem (the kind bank wraps to 3 rows), the scope is 7.75rem, each distance sits on its own line after a break with the cursor after the last one, text-wrap is balance, and the 'North at the top…' sentence is kept for screen readers but drawn by the scope's own lettering (an 'N' at the top plus the 15m/45m/2h rings). Clear sits at the end of the Search label's line, so it costs no height.

Phone and tablet (<64rem): the console div becomes display:contents. Its head and its answer each become their own glass panel, ordered head, then desk, then answer. On Ideas at 390px the title is at y 465 (was about 870) and the radar sits under the list. The console is a plain div, and its named parts are a search form (role=search, aria-label), navs and an aside, so display:contents drops no landmark. Each bank is a sideways strip with a fade mask. The latched key is brought into view with scroll-initial-target instead of order:-1, so visual and tab order agree: TRIP latched gives scrollLeft 685.

Grounded colour: slate means choose or go, indigo means act, green means send. Home's section links became slate, so indigo there is only the three starters and the mic, and Send is the one green key.

The phosphor stays at full strength wherever there is a tube. screen is #6dff9c with screenGlow 1.0. --shadow is 0 0 #0000, so the base glows survive. The new tubes (tally, settings readout, form radar) all come from the crt macro, so they get scanlines, 0.35px blur, layered halos, the roll bar, the power light and the cursor. The primary key keeps its ring and pool on the 1.2s afterglow. The live lamps breathe. Slate keys, rows and cards stay matte.

Every link bank keeps its field names and endpoints, and removed.txt is empty. Word changes: 'Skip to the list' on Ideas and To do, 'View' on Plans, To do's due words, and the Open/Done tag dropped from rows unless Show is All.

firstDraft.name: Tuning Dock
firstDraft.concept: Docked Terminal took two big steps. Its lit glass column is now a console, and the same rule holds on every page: the keys you use to tune the desk sit at the head of the console, and the machine's answer sits at its foot. On Home that is the box, then Next up. On Ideas it is a bank of latching keys, then the radar. On To do it is the Show keys, then the count on the glass. The whole app now uses one type scale, a perfect fourth with six steps, and every size on every page is one of them. The page should feel like a calm terminal on a desk at night. Pressing a key latches it, the tubes glow at full phosphor, and the slate mat stays quiet.

designs.name: Evening Listing, Relit
designs.tagline: Evening Listing with the tube switched back on where the machine is live, lines drawn only where there is an order, and a head column that always says how things stand.
designs.concept: This is Evening Listing's programme guide kept whole: slate bands with a head column, one-line rows read along a leader to tabular facts, and steel reverse video for "here". What comes back is the original tube's light, and only on a short list of what is live: the mark, "mind", Send, the box, the Now lamp, the status lamps, the monitors and her screen. Everything the family keeps stays matte. Lines appear only where there is an order, and every head column now says how its band stands. The feel is an evening TV listing lit by one real green tube: calm and easy to scan, with light exactly where the eye should go.
designs.companions: The companion colours are unchanged from Evening Listing, but each now has a clearer job. Steel #7a93a8 (lifted from #748a9b) with a #a9c4d8 cap means "here" everywhere: the bar, the view switches in the head columns, the kind key, the Settings nav, today on the month and the phone tab. A darker steel #58697a draws the only lines: Coming up's rail and stops, the Chat rail and dateline tick, and the family's bubble cap. Denim #9db6d6 is every link that is words. Pewter-slate bands (#10161a, zebra #161d22) carry all the listings. Cobalt #4f60e6 at 2.4 sits in the greeting's far corner. Sage #86d9a6 is for everyday lit things: a ticked box, a field's edge while typing, "Now", the 2px edge of a row's afterglow. Amber appears only as rings and text, never as a fill: the numbered setup rings, "late", a late task's tick-well edge, and "needs a look". Kind colours are mixed 72% toward the ink, so lemon and amber no longer read as neon. The exact #6dff9c is kept for the lit list.
decisions: Light as a list, per the kit: screen #6dff9c at screenGlow 1.0, glow .9, topGlow 1.0, washGlow 2.4. Because the css is not re-tinted, I wrote E1 ('mind'), E2 (tile halo, icon drop-shadow, caret), E3 (--glow ring and pool, hover on the primaries only), E4 (Home's box glowing at rest, and every field being typed in with a 3px ring and a 22px bloom), E12 (80px spill and a two-layer LED) and E20 (lamps) as color-mix of var(--brand)/--phosphor at full value. --shadow is 0 0 #0000, not none. --afterglow is 1.2s and --glow-in .12s.

The green pool rises from under Send: its radial centre is computed from the grid, calc(100% - pad - 21.5rem - gap - 3rem), and the masked scanlines follow it. The box is translucent again (rgb(9 12 11/.72)). The pixel 1px under Send reads (37,82,53) against today's (37,80,52).

Tubes brought back to today's size: VT323 on a written tube scale of 2 for the one title, 1.5 for lines and 1.2 at least. To keep 'Tuesday 29 September,' on one line at 1.5, I floated Next up's radar with shape-outside (as the phone already does). The radar is 5.6rem, so the words run round the scope.

Lit current page: the steel block gets an inset 2px #a9c4d8 cap, and under it the tuning scale's segment is #6dff9c with a 6px halo. The title tile gets back its raster and a small glow (18px -6px at 55%) in its section colour. Vera's bubble has no glow at rest.

Lines only where there is order. The L-bracket and the page-icon rings are gone. (a) Coming up, on Home and on the Plans list, has a 1px #58697a rail down the designator column. It starts at a breathing 9px Now lamp labelled NOW in Plex Mono .75, has a 7px steel stop at each date leaf (lighter on today), and ends at the last one. (b) Setup steps are 1-2-3 Plex Mono numerals in amber rings, joined by one hairline. I had to neutralise the base stylesheet's .setup li::before ring, which was turning the line into drips. (c) Chat follows Track Diagram: the rail drops from her title screen (the chat page head's column is set so the tile sits on the rail), runs through her screen at each of her lines, and ends at a lit ring at the box. The date is set once as a dateline with a tick. Each time hangs beside its bubble. The family is on the right, on square #1f272e with a steel cap and square steel initials. The amber avatar discs are gone, so amber keeps its one job.

Head columns always hold something. Every band head has a Plex Mono tabular .875 summary: '4 more / next in 2 days', '4 open / 2 late' (late in amber), '12 ideas', '0 open', lamp tallies on Status ('3 on / 1 off'), '9 parts / 1 to look at' on Settings, and '1 plan / in September' on the month. Ideas has a 2rem figure over IDEAS, the All ideas/Restaurants switch as vertical steel cells, and a 9-entry kind key. Each key entry is a link to /ideas?kind=X that keeps the other filters, and a second press clears it. To do has the figure, late in amber, and Open/Done/Cancelled/All links doing the Show select's GET. The Plans List/Month switch moved into the head column too, so one rule holds on every page. A head column with no h2 starts flush.

To do marks late from the app clock (config.FAMILYDB_APP.clock.today()). A small macro reproduces views.relative_text using date ordinals ('was due 2 days ago' in amber, 'due in 2 days, 19:56'). A late tick well gets a 1.5px amber edge. OPEN is hidden under Show=Open. A reminder shows only when there is one ('reminds 30 Sep 09:00'), and 'No active reminder.' stays for screen readers only. The search is on one line with Filter.

Row afterglow: a 2px sage edge plus a 12% steel wash, drawn as an inset box-shadow so it layers over zebra and bare rows alike. It comes on in .12s. I bent the brief from 8% to 12%, and fade it on an ease-in-out 'linger' curve (1.2s cubic-bezier(.45,0,.55,1)) instead of the kit's ease-out, because the ease-out finished before the strip's 380ms frame. The strip now shows it at 120, 380 and fading by 900ms.

Written type scale as tokens: .75 caps/labels, .875 detail and facts, 1 body/rows, 1.125 lede and h2/h3, 1.3 band heads, 2 the question and figures, 2.75 the masthead. I audited computed sizes on 14 pages with my own Playwright script and put the stragglers on the scale: the bar labels, hints, .small, section states, ghost buttons, the footer legal line (now sans .75) and the phone tab labels. Plex Mono carries the zero and tnum features. h3 is now a sans 1.125 head, not a .72 mono-caps label, so no head ranks below its rows (the Wishes lists read 'Every day', 'Christmas'). Vera's date is 'TUE 29 SEP', nowrap, with the full date for screen readers. The FROM label and the date are no longer VT323: VT323 now lives only on glass.

I kept mono caps for field and column labels (SEARCH, KIND, FROM, NOW). The brief says 'Plex Mono for figures only'. My reason: these are the machine's one- or two-word legends, not sentences. All sentences ('4 shown (up to 100).', the legal line) moved to the sans.

Usability: Memory, Family and Status show words from 75rem (they fit at 1280). The Status lamp rows are capped at 62rem. On Status, only 'Who answers' and 'Connected to' breathe; keys that are set glow still. 0 targets under 44px on all 13 renders. The Ideas Tab order is bar, then Add an idea (12), All ideas (13), Restaurants (14), the kinds (15-23), then the finder, which matches the drawing. Home is 1643px.

Beyond the brief, so the rule holds on pages outside the sheets: Wishes renders each kid as a band, with the name and the open-count link in the head column. Phone Ideas rows put the facts under the title; they used to wrap the title into four lines. Reduced motion stops the lamps and transitions. More contrast drops the halos, scanlines and tube blur (the kit's MC block, plus mine for the rules I restate) and keeps the lamps' glow, as the kit says.

designs.name: Long Persistence
designs.tagline: The phosphor draws, the page prints: each page has one lit instrument that traces the family's own weeks, due dates or places with full bloom and afterglow, and every row of the graphite legend under it lights its mark.
designs.concept: The light is the data. Each page with something in time or space gets one 4:3 P1 tube in a thin graphite case, and the tube draws that page's own data with the original's full effect: bloom, a 0.35px blur, scanlines, sheen, falloff, an 80px spill, a sweep beam with a wake of afterglow, and glowing marks that flare as the beam passes and never go out. Everything else is print: legend tables on graphite in bone ink with no glow. Pointing at a row lights its mark on the tube in 0.12s, and it fades over 1.2s. The page feels calmer and more grounded, and the green-screen tube is back, now doing a job: light only where attention belongs.
designs.companions: Steel-blue print carries the calm. The accent #84a0c4 marks Home, Status and Settings. Links are chalk blue #a9bfd8, underlined, in sentence case. The column heads and labels are #a8b2bc. "Here" is a #7c96b0 reverse block with a #aec6dc cap, used in the bar, the tabs, the Settings nav, the phone tab bar, the chosen picker option and today on the month. The family's chat bubbles are #1d2429 under a 2px chalk cap. Graphite solids hold every table: surface #14191c, a zebra step #171c20 and hairlines #1f2529. The cases are graphite #2c3135 with engraved #a3acb3 chin legends. The ink is bone: #d5cfc3 for body text and #ece6d8 for headings. One cobalt light, #4f60e6 at washGlow 2.2, sits in the greeting's top-right corner. Section and kind colours keep their learned values. Kinds show only on small tiles, 14% for cool kinds and 6% for warm, with the kind word mixed 72% with ink. Amber appears only as rings or edges (setup steps, "needs a look") and as late text. Red is kept for off. Inside the tubes there is only phosphor.
decisions: THE RULE is written at the head of the css: 'The phosphor draws; the page prints.' Main-lane palette: 45.3k characters appended to today's stylesheet, so every kit effect (E1-E22) is inherited and re-tinted. The palette's own templates are in variants/r11-idea-2/templates. build.py compresses palette.css into the JSON and generates the per-key rules.

Home. The scope replaces the Next up radar and keeps .next-up. The glass carries VT323 text: an inverse NEXT UP, the title, TUE 29 SEP 17:00 [TODAY], and '> 4 more on the scope'. Under the text, the trace covers the next four weeks at 1 wk/div: a bright trigger at NOW on the left edge, one pulse per day with plans (one step taller per plan), the next plan intensified with a ping ring, day numerals, a dotted OCT month-turn cursor, and an overrange arrow. Each day offset comes from the app clock (config.FAMILYDB_APP.clock.today() with date.replace), and pulses sit at the plan's time of day. This is simpler than Bench Scope's civil() and needs no year inference.

Deviation: the graticule is 4x3, not 10x8. At 1 wk/div, a 10-division screen would show ten weeks and crowd four weeks of plans into its left 40%. With 4x3, one square division is one week and each minor tick on the centre line is one day. The centre cross is at 18% and the grid at 10%, as briefed.

Sweep. A 1px #e4fff0 beam with a 6px halo and a masked afterglow wake crosses every 8s. Each mark's flare uses a delay class (t0-t40) derived from its x position, so it flares exactly as the beam passes, then settles to 0.3 (0.62 for the next plan). I start the beam 1.6s into its cycle so the motion strips and the stills catch it mid-glass, with the marks it has already passed still glowing. It was hard to see at the rim otherwise.

Keyed rows. Each mark is a wrapper holding two layers: an animated .flare and an un-animated .lit layer. Rows and marks share a class (k0-k27 and kfar by day offset on Home and Plans; r1-r40 by row position on Ideas and To do). CSS cannot match two elements by an arbitrary shared value, so there is one rule per key. I keyed Ideas and To do by row position instead of by id because positions are bounded and ids grow forever. Verified: hovering the Oct 9 row lit its pulse, and hovering row 3 on Ideas lit the Silver Falls blip.

To do gets a due scope: -14 to +14 days at 1 wk/div, with the trigger at NOW in the centre. There is one tick per dated open task (#id on top), and nearby ticks are staggered. Ideas. The XY radar runs at full (sweep, afterglow, glowing blips, the nearest pinging) with its readout beside it, inside the tube. It turns amber at 75% and red at 100% through --phosphor, as today. I moved the 'Today: about $0.00 ... Change the limit' sentence up beside it, so the head is not an empty block. Chat. Her screen is the instrument: 3.5rem at the head, with bloom and a scan mask. The glyphs fall while a pending line is thinking. Print. Every list is a legend table. The column-head row is set in Archivo wdth 112, weight 600, 0.75rem caps with 0.05em tracking in the label colour, over a 1px rule. After ten rounds colour has settled. Every winner sits in the same lane: a green-black ground, cool low-chroma slate or steel in solids that have a job, bone ink near 12.5:1, amber with its one job, and the exact #6dff9c. Every warm, wine, teal, violet, serif, lifted-ground, caps-button and dots-for-here roll has lost. Structure, typesetting, usability and now light decide.

## Round 11

Top four by score: r11-idea-1 Evening Listing, Relit 8.04; r11-idea-2 Long Persistence 7.88; r11-mut-4 Track Diagram Relit 7.52; r10-idea-1 Evening Listing 7.12.

- WHY WINNERS WON. Evening Listing, Relit (in 8 top fours) is the first entrant whose head column does a job on every page: counts and late on Home, the kind filter on Ideas, Open/Done/Cancelled on To do, List/Month on Plans, on/off on Status. That solves round 10's empty-column problem with type ('12 IDEAS', '4 OPEN / 2 late'). Long Persistence (7 top fours, 7 promise votes) added true column heads (WHO, DUE) with right-aligned tabular figures, and tubes that draw the family's own weeks and spending. Both have 0 small targets, words in the bar and amber 'was due' on To do. Relighting (#6dff9c, screenGlow 1.0, bloom and spill) beat every unlit carried parent at full size, but only where the light stayed on the short list of live things. Refines round 10: relighting is visible at page scale only when it lights something new. Track Diagram Relit won the feedback and soul lenses (8.8, 8.2) through its lit stretch of track from the now lamp, but style and skeptic called it near-invisible in stills where it only brightened existing lamps. It also lost usability for dropping the 'was due' words, leaving late as colour and position only.
- LOSSES AND COLOURS. The skeptic sampled the olive-bronze setup tray, which survives as warm grey fills: (19,22,18) in the Track family and (18,20,16) in the Signal family. Only Evening Listing, Relit, Long Persistence and Blueprint Terminal held setup to neutral slate with amber rings or edges. Fixes for the leader: darken the steel 'here' block from about #7a93a8 to #5f7689, keeping its #a9c4d8 cap. Make the afterglow a 10-14% steel wash with a 2px sage (#86d9a6) edge that fades over 1-1.2s; it is still invisible in almost every capture (open problem, third round). Blueprint Terminal's paper 'here' block was the brightest non-green thing on the page; drop it to about #a9ab9f or steel. Its periwinkle links (#94bbfe) should go to #9fb4d6. The blue-led entrants (Tuning Dock, Blueprint, Docked) still spend blue on keys and tiles; indigo belongs on the one latched key per bank. Parent/child near-duplicates (for example Evening Listing beside its Relit child, 7.12 against 8.04) wasted slots. The child won in every pair, so carry the child, not both.
- FAILED REACHES. (1) Flight Console (6.67, 7 promise) had a period instrument language: a zero-padded readout strip, flight-plan arcs, an annunciator, a crew board, T-minus setup, a flight-log chat and a warm-up with green card afterglow. It failed on tracked mono caps for the nav and 'ALL →' links, 23 small targets, amber with two jobs, an annunciator that repeats the Status lists, FIG captions and a one-sided Chat. To try again, make the readout strip a global row of 44px links (LATE to To do filtered, PLANS to Plans), with sentence-case labels, Plex Mono figures and today in steel. (2) Videotex Sommaire (5.98, 5 promise) typed the question on the glass under a blinking cursor, had a warm-up from a line, lit an LED on the current key and opened on a numbered Contents with leaders to counts. The panel called these the round's most faithful return of the CRT soul and its best 'what is on this page' device. It failed on a brown plastic case, VT323 on band heads, five pastel filled tiles, nav moved to a foot key row, setup placed last, 35 small targets and a 3574px Home. To try again, use a graphite case (#2c3135) and keep VT323 on the glass and page tiles only. Heads go in condensed Instrument Sans 600 at about 1.5rem, the tiles become one neutral tile with a 3px section cap, and the nav stays in the top bar. (3) Night Gallery (5.67) hung a picture light over each monitor, the most elegant scarcity idea, and used bone ink with brass wall labels. It lost on a one-size type system, sideways titles, brass tracked caps and an olive tray. Add a 34-40px question and title step. (4) Signal Legend, Drawn (6.68, 2 promise) drew engraved line pictures. Make them a system: one per page head and for empty states, about 48px with 1.75px lines, alongside the icons, not in place of them.
- TRAITS. There were no random seeds this round (seeds.json is empty), so the protected random slot has no evidence. The informed entrants took 1st and 2nd. The phosphor mutant Track Diagram Relit (7.52) beat its carried parent (7.00). The type mutant Track Diagram, Large Setting (7.11, parent 7.00) had a 17px/1.6 body and a five-step written scale, which feedback and type want bred into the leader. Its prose cards wrapped at that size, and its kind words sat at 13px, below the text. Rewarded: a 15px step between body and the 12px floor, and a one-line row with a tabular column. The graphics mutant Signal Legend, Drawn (6.68, below its parent's 6.91) lost for taking icons off the bar, the phone tab bar and the mic. Its engraved drawings were liked but were too thin at 100%. So pictures that replace icons lose, and pictures added beside them may win. The crossover Blueprint Terminal (6.71) kept the machine column, a status foot and a late-bar tube on To do, the round's best late signal. It lost on a non-sticky full-height lit column (light becoming a wash, dead black), blueprint tiles on every row and the paper 'here' block. The wild mutant Tuning Dock (6.76) won interaction and usability (7.8, 8.0) with a sticky-able dock of one-tap latched banks. It lost on indigo starters, caps keys for links and a non-sticky dock. The wild entrants all changed the whole page but broke held rules. Faces rewarded: condensed Instrument Sans heads, Plex Mono figures only, tabular right-aligned columns, playscript and flight-log chats. Not rewarded: VT323 off the glass, pixel item names (Pocket Timeline), tracked or extended caps on controls, and a single size.
- LIGHT AS DATA. This is new. The judges preferred a tube that draws something (Long Persistence's weeks, Blueprint's late bars, the plan trace) to one that glows brighter. Empty lit glass was faulted everywhere: Next up's tube stretched past its words on the leader, and Blueprint's column ran to the foot. Fixes: size the tube to its words with align-self:start, or fill spare glass with a fortnight trace. Long Persistence's sweep beam must not cross text, and its resting pulses need to be taller and brighter, with the next one labelled on the glass.
- ONE CONTROL PER FILTER. Evening Listing, Relit's kind list duplicated the Kind select (Restaurants appeared twice), and its kind key grew to nine 44px cells. Fix: keep the head-column list as the only kind filter, set it two-up, and drop the select. Head summaries that repeat their rows ('0 open' over two '0 open' rows) cost points. State cells should be links ('2 late' goes to To do filtered).
- CANDIDATE PRINCIPLES. (a) Every list names its facts, by a head column that states how the band stands or by column heads, and late is amber words on Home and To do, never colour alone. (b) Phosphor light is information: a lit tube draws or holds live data sized to its content, and no glass is lit that is empty. (c) The bar names every place in words, and controls and see-more links are sentence case; tracked caps are kept for eyebrows, legends and speakers.
